definition_zh: 远缘繁殖；远交；与亲缘较远的个体交配繁殖
definition_en: breeding between individuals that are not closely related, especially in order to increase genetic variation in the offspring
core_image: 两片相距很远的林地里的个体被牵到一起，把各自的血统带进同一个后代
scene: 育种站把来自两片相距很远的林地的个体配到一起，用远缘繁殖提高后代的遗传多样性。 At the breeding station, individuals from two woodlands far apart are paired in outbreeding to raise the genetic diversity of their offspring.
sceneCN: 这里 outbreeding 是「与亲缘关系较远的个体交配繁殖」（第 1 个义项：远缘个体之间的配对繁殖）；句意：育种站把来自两片相距很远林地的个体配到一起，用远缘繁殖提高后代的遗传多样性。

pos.zh: 远缘繁殖；远交（与近亲繁殖相对，多作不可数）

senses.title: Mate with a distantly related partner
senses.titleCN: 与亲缘较远的个体交配
senses.definition: to breed with an individual that is not a close relative, so that the young receive genes from two separate lines
senses.definitionCN: 与并非近亲的个体繁殖，使后代获得来自两条独立血统的基因
senses.example: Zoos plan outbreeding to keep captive herds healthy.
senses.exampleCN: 动物园规划远缘交配，以保持圈养群体的健康。
senses.why: Out- is the native English prefix for 'outside, beyond', so outbreeding names mating that reaches outside the circle of close kin; the compound is English, not Latin.
senses.whyCN: out- 是英语本族前缀，意为「在外、超出」，因此 outbreeding 指把配对对象选到近亲圈之外；这个词是英语复合词，并非拉丁借词。

senses.title: Raise heterozygosity in genetics
senses.definition: in genetics, the mating of unrelated individuals so that many gene loci become heterozygous in the offspring
senses.definitionCN: 遗传学中让无亲缘个体交配，使后代许多基因座位呈杂合状态
senses.example: Outbreeding raised heterozygosity at loci that had been fixed in the isolated herd.
senses.exampleCN: 远缘交配使这个隔离群体中原本固定的基因座位变为杂合。
senses.why: Genetics borrowed the word and made it quantitative: the further apart the parents, the more loci arrive heterozygous, so the term now names a genetic effect rather than a pedigree.
senses.whyCN: 遗传学借用了这个词并使它可以量化：亲本相距越远，后代杂合的座位越多，因此这个词现在指一种遗传效应，而不只是谱系关系。

senses.title: A livestock breeding practice
senses.titleCN: 家畜育种中的一项做法
senses.definition: the practice of bringing an unrelated sire or dam into a herd to refresh its bloodlines
senses.definitionCN: 把无亲缘的公畜或母畜引入畜群、以更新其血统的做法
senses.example: Cattle breeders use outbreeding to bring new bloodlines into a closed herd.
senses.exampleCN: 养牛者用远缘交配把新的血统引入封闭的畜群。
senses.why: Herd books set inbreeding against outbreeding to describe breeding plans, and the word settled into the vocabulary of livestock improvement.
senses.whyCN: 畜群登记簿用近交与远交对举来描述繁殖计划，这个词于是进入了家畜改良的术语体系。

senses.title: Crossing inbred lines in plant breeding
senses.titleCN: 植物育种中杂交自交系
senses.definition: in plant breeding, the crossing of genetically distinct inbred lines to obtain vigorous hybrids
senses.definitionCN: 植物育种中把遗传上不同的自交系杂交，以获得长势旺盛的杂种
senses.example: Plant breeders rely on outbreeding when two inbred lines are crossed.
senses.exampleCN: 植物育种者把两个自交系杂交时，依靠的正是远缘繁殖。
senses.why: Plant breeders also say outcrossing for the same act; outbreeding is the general term, and the two are often used side by side in applied genetics.
senses.whyCN: 植物育种者也用 outcrossing 指同一做法；outbreeding 是总称，二者在应用遗传学文献里常并列使用。

senses.title: A remedy for inbreeding depression
senses.definition: the introduction of unrelated mates into a small isolated population whose fitness has fallen through inbreeding
senses.definitionCN: 向因近交而适合度下降的小型隔离群体引入无亲缘配偶
senses.example: Conservationists recommend outbreeding once the island population shows inbreeding depression.
senses.exampleCN: 一旦岛上群体出现近交衰退，保护工作者就建议采用远缘交配。
senses.why: Conservation biology reversed the old assumption that any crossing is good: outbreeding is prescribed when a small population shows inbreeding depression.
senses.whyCN: 保护生物学纠正了过去「任何杂交都好」的假设：只有当小群体出现近交衰退时，才指定采用远缘交配。

senses.title: The technical opposite of inbreeding
senses.titleCN: 与近亲繁殖构成的技术对立项
senses.definition: the mating pattern defined chiefly by contrast with inbreeding, namely pairing outside rather than inside the family line
senses.definitionCN: 主要指与近亲繁殖相对立的交配方式，即在家族线之外而非之内配对
senses.example: The pedigree records both inbreeding and outbreeding across five generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这份谱系记录跨越五代，把近交与远交都记了下来。
senses.why: The word exists mainly as the opposite of inbreeding, so its meaning is fixed by the contrast: mate outside the family line rather than inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词主要通过作为 inbreeding 的反义词而存在，其意义由对比确定：在家族线外交配，而不是在内。

senses.title: Outbreeding depression: too distant is harmful
senses.titleCN: 远交衰退：过远反而有害
senses.definition: a loss of fitness in hybrids whose parents came from populations carrying incompatible gene combinations
senses.definitionCN: 亲本来自携带不相容基因组合的群体时，杂种适合度下降的现象
senses.example: Outbreeding can lower fitness when distant populations carry incompatible gene complexes.
senses.exampleCN: 当相距很远的群体携带不相容的基因组合时，远缘交配可能降低适合度。
senses.why: Because distant populations may carry incompatible gene complexes, outbreeding has a negative branch, outbreeding depression, where hybrid fitness falls.
senses.whyCN: 由于相距很远的群体可能携带不相容的基因组合，远缘交配有一个负面分支，即远交衰退：杂种的适合度反而下降。

senses.title: A natural mating pattern in the wild
senses.definition: a mating pattern produced without a breeder, for example by dispersal or by mate choice that avoids relatives
senses.definitionCN: 无需育种者介入、由扩散或避开亲属的择偶行为形成的交配格局
senses.example: Dispersal serves as a natural outbreeding mechanism in many wind-pollinated plants.
senses.exampleCN: 对许多风媒植物来说，扩散就是天然的远缘繁殖机制。
senses.why: In wild plants and animals, dispersal and mate choice perform outbreeding without a breeder, so the term also names a natural mating pattern.
senses.whyCN: 在野生动植物中，扩散与择偶无需育种者即可完成远缘交配，因此这个词也指一种自然交配格局。

intro.en: Outbreeding is a native English compound, not a Latin borrowing: out- 'outside' plus breeding, from Old English brēdan 'to brood, hatch'. No Latin relative exists, so latinEntries is left empty. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: outbreeding 是英语本族复合词，并非拉丁借词：out-「在外」加 breeding，后者源自古英语 brēdan「孵、育」。本词没有拉丁同族，因此拉丁同族词条列表留空。年代均为约数。

items.en: The native verb brēdan meant 'to brood, to hatch, to warm', and its derivative brēding gave the noun breeding 'the act of producing young'.
items.cn: 本族动词 brēdan 意为「孵、抱窝、使暖」，其派生形式 brēding 给出名词 breeding「育幼的行为」。

items.en: By the Middle English period breeding covered the raising of animals and plants as well as hatching, and the sense 'reproduction controlled by humans' was in place.
items.cn: 到中古英语时期，breeding 已不仅指孵卵，还指饲养动植物，「由人控制繁殖」的意思也已经出现。

items.en: Out- is the native prefix meaning 'outside, beyond'; it marks the direction of the mating, away from the close family circle.
items.cn: out- 是英语本族前缀，意为「在外、超出」；它标出交配的方向，即离开近亲圈。

items.en: Nineteenth-century herd books set inbreeding against outbreeding, and the contrast fixed the word in livestock breeding.
items.cn: 19 世纪的畜群登记簿把近交与远交对举，这一对比使该词在家畜育种中固定下来。

items.en: Twentieth-century genetics made outbreeding a measurable event: the pairing of unrelated individuals to raise heterozygosity and mask recessive defects.
items.cn: 20 世纪遗传学使远缘繁殖成为可测量的事件：让无亲缘个体配对，以提高杂合度、掩盖隐性缺陷。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact year when the compound outbreeding first appeared in print is not established here, and no Latin source exists for the word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：outbreeding 这一复合词最早见于印刷品的确切年份此处无法确定；该词也没有拉丁语来源。

note.en: Group one holds the breeding terms that are constantly confused; group two holds near neighbours that name a crossing or its result.
note.cn: 第一组是极易混淆的繁殖术语；第二组是表示杂交行为或其结果、语义相近的词。

entries.definition: Breeding between close relatives. In- 'inside' marks mating within the family line, exactly the direction outbreeding avoids.
entries.definitionCN: 近亲之间的繁殖。in-「在内」标出家族线之内的交配，正是 outbreeding 所要避开的方向。

entries.definition: The crossing of two unrelated lines, the usual term in plant and animal breeding for what outbreeding names in general.
entries.definitionCN: 两个无亲缘品系的杂交，是动植物育种中对应 outbreeding 总称的常用具体说法。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun: to mate an individual with one outside its close kin. Outbreeding is simply the action noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词：使个体与近亲圈之外的个体交配。outbreeding 只是该动作的名词形式。

entries.definition: Crossing between different breeds or varieties, not necessarily distant relatives. It is broader in scope than outbreeding.
entries.definitionCN: 不同品种或变种之间的杂交，亲缘未必很远；范围比 outbreeding 更宽。

entries.definition: The production of hybrids, often between different species. Outbreeding normally stays within one species.
entries.definitionCN: 产生杂种的过程，常指不同物种之间；outbreeding 通常仍在同一物种内。

entries.definition: Deliberate mating to a particular ancestor's line, a controlled form of inbreeding rather than its opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 有意向某一祖先血统靠拢的配种，是受控的近交形式，而非其反面。

entries.definition: The movement of genes from one population or species into another through repeated crossing. It names the genetic result, not the breeding plan.
entries.definitionCN: 基因通过反复杂交从一个群体或物种流入另一个。它指遗传结果，而非配种方案。

entries.definition: The variety of alleles in a population, which outbreeding is used to raise; it is the aim, not the method.
entries.definitionCN: 群体中等位基因的多样性，正是远缘繁殖所要提高的对象；它是目的，不是方法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: out- 'outside' + breeding: mating that reaches outside the close family circle.
normal.cn: out-「在外」+ breeding：把配对对象选到近亲圈之外。

normal.en: The herd-book pair is inbreeding versus outbreeding, so the two words define each other.
normal.cn: 畜群登记簿里的对举是 inbreeding 与 outbreeding，两个词互相定义。

normal.en: Applied genetics also says outcrossing; the two terms often stand side by side in breeding manuals.
normal.cn: 应用遗传学也说 outcrossing；两个术语在育种手册里常并列出现。

normal.en: The negative branch has its own name: outbreeding depression, the mirror image of hybrid vigour.
normal.cn: 负面分支有自己的名称：outbreeding depression 远交衰退，正好与杂种优势相对。

normal.en: Outbreed, outbred and outbreeder are the verb, the participle and the person noun of the same family.
normal.cn: outbreed、outbred 与 outbreeder 是同一词族的动词、分词与施事名词。

abstract.en: Picture two orchards on opposite hills sending pollen to each other across the valley.
abstract.cn: 想象两座相对山坡上的果园隔着河谷互相送粉。

abstract.en: Picture a locked herd book with a new page ruled for a stranger's line.
abstract.cn: 想象一本锁着的畜群登记簿翻出新的一页，留给外来血统。

abstract.en: Picture a small island population that stops weakening once outsiders arrive.
abstract.cn: 想象一个海岛小群体，在外来个体到来后不再衰弱。

examples.en: The recovery plan set a minimum outbreeding distance between the two reserves.
examples.cn: 恢复计划为两个保护区之间规定了最小的远交距离。

examples.en: Too much outbreeding can break up gene combinations that local conditions had favoured.
examples.cn: 远缘交配过度会拆散本地环境原本偏爱的基因组合。

examples.en: Farmers describe outbreeding simply as bringing in a new bull from another district.
examples.cn: 农户把远缘繁殖简单说成从别的地区引进一头新公牛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特的育种」——把外头的血统引进来 → outbreeding 远缘繁殖

root: 英语本族复合词：out-（在外、向外）+ breeding（繁殖，源自古英语 brēdan「孵、育」）；无拉丁词根，拉丁同族词条列表留空。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of outbreeding all describe one move: a mate is brought in from outside the circle of close kin, and the effects of that move are then read in pedigrees, in heterozygosity, in hybrid vigour and finally in its failure.
sensesIntro.cn: outbreeding 的八个义项都描述同一个动作：从近亲圈之外引入配偶，随后这一动作的后果被分别读成谱系记录、杂合度、杂种优势，最后是它的失败。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two separate bloodlines meeting in one offspring, with the family circle left behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条彼此分离的血统在一个后代身上会合，近亲圈被留在身后。

branches.en: THE DEFINITION BY CONTRAST: outbreeding is what inbreeding is not, so the pair fixes the meaning.
branches.cn: 以对比定义：远缘繁殖就是近交的反面，两个词互为定义。

branches.en: MEASURABLE MIXING: genetics turns the pedigree move into a count of heterozygous loci.
branches.cn: 可测量的混合：遗传学把谱系上的动作变成杂合座位的计数。

branches.en: APPLIED CROSSING: plant breeders cross inbred lines and harvest the vigour.
branches.cn: 应用杂交：植物育种者杂交自交系，收获杂种优势。

branches.en: TWO OUTCOMES: bringing in outsiders can rescue a small population or break up co-adapted genes.
branches.cn: 两种结局：引入外来者既能挽救小群体，也可能拆散共适应的基因组合。

branches.en: WILD COUNTERPART: dispersal does the breeder's work without a breeder.
branches.cn: 野外的对应机制：扩散在没有育种者时完成了育种者的事。

intro.en: Outbreeding is a native compound whose two parts are both transparent English morphemes; the list shows how each part and each relative behaves.
intro.cn: outbreeding 是本族复合词，两个部分都是透明的英语语素；下表逐个说明各成分与同族词的作用。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin counterpart: it is formed from native English stock, so latinEntries is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词没有拉丁语对应成分，由英语本族词素构成，因此拉丁同族词条列表留空。

items.example: Out- sends the mating outside the close family circle.
items.exampleCN: out- 把交配方向送到近亲圈之外。

items.example: Breeding is the general act that outbreeding qualifies.
items.exampleCN: breeding 是远缘繁殖所限定的那个总动作。

items.meaning: to mate outside the close kin
items.example: Keepers outbreed the captive group every third generation.
items.exampleCN: 饲养者每三代为圈养群体做一次远交。

items.example: The outbred pups were heavier at birth.
items.exampleCN: 远交产生的幼崽出生时更重。

items.meaning: a breeder or an individual that mates out
items.example: The outbreeder matched animals from different valleys.
items.exampleCN: 这位远交育种者把不同河谷的动物配对。

items.example: Inbreeding raised the frequency of a recessive defect.
items.exampleCN: 近交提高了隐性缺陷的出现频率。

items.example: Outcrossing restored yield in the depleted variety.
items.exampleCN: 异系交配恢复了衰退品种的产量。

items.example: Crossbreeding of two cattle breeds is common in the region.
items.exampleCN: 两个牛品种的杂交在该地区很常见。

definition_zh: 物种形成；新物种的产生
definition_en: the process by which new biological species arise from existing populations
core_image: 一条河把同一群鸟分成两岸两支，许多代以后它们再相遇却已不再互认
scene: 一条宽阔的河流改道，把同一群鸟分成东西两支，长期隔离之后它们逐渐形成不同的物种，这一过程就是物种形成。 A wide river changed course and split one bird population into an eastern and a western branch; after long isolation they gradually became different species, a process called speciation.
sceneCN: 这里 speciation 是「物种形成」（第 1 个义项：新物种从既有群体中分出的整个过程）；句意：河流改道把同一群鸟分成东西两支，长期隔离后逐渐形成不同物种，这一过程叫物种形成。

pos.zh: 物种形成；物种分化（不可数）

derivatives.zh: 形成物种；发生物种分化

senses.title: The rise of a new species
senses.definition: the whole process by which a lineage splits into distinct species that no longer share one gene pool
senses.definitionCN: 一个谱系分化为若干不再共享同一基因库的物种的整个过程
senses.example: Speciation begins when gene flow between two populations stops.
senses.exampleCN: 当两个群体之间的基因流停止时，物种形成便开始了。
senses.why: Species plus -ation makes a noun of process: the category 'kind' is turned into the event of a new kind coming into being.
senses.whyCN: species 加 -ation 构成过程名词：把「种类」这一范畴变成「新种类产生」这一事件。

senses.title: Allopatric speciation by geography
senses.titleCN: 异域物种形成：地理隔离导致分化
senses.definition: speciation that follows when a physical barrier divides one population into separate ranges
senses.definitionCN: 物理屏障把一个群体分隔到不同分布区之后发生的物种形成
senses.example: Allopatric speciation began when the valley cut the population in two.
senses.exampleCN: 当河谷把这个群体切成两半时，异域物种形成开始了。
senses.why: Allo- 'other' plus patria 'fatherland' names the geography: each daughter population evolves in another homeland.
senses.whyCN: allo-「别的」加 patria「故土」点明地理条件：每个子群体都在另一片故土中演化。

senses.title: Sympatric speciation without a barrier
senses.titleCN: 同域物种形成：无地理屏障
senses.definition: speciation within one continuous area, driven by factors such as polyploidy, host shift or assortative mating
senses.definitionCN: 在同一连续区域内，由多倍化、寄主转换或选型交配等因素驱动的物种形成
senses.example: Sympatric speciation can follow a shift to a new host plant.
senses.exampleCN: 同域物种形成可以随着转向新的寄主植物而发生。
senses.why: Syn- 'together' plus patria 'homeland' says the opposite of the allopatric case: the two forms diverge while living in the same place.
senses.whyCN: syn-「共同」加 patria「故土」与异域情形正好相反：两个类型在同一地点生活却发生分化。

senses.title: Parapatric speciation along a gradient
senses.titleCN: 邻域物种形成：沿环境梯度分化
senses.definition: speciation across a partial barrier or a steep environmental gradient, with limited gene flow at the contact zone
senses.definitionCN: 在部分屏障或陡峭环境梯度两侧发生的物种形成，接触带仍有有限的基因流
senses.example: Parapatric speciation proceeds along the steep gradient of the mountain slope.
senses.exampleCN: 邻域物种形成沿着山坡陡峭的环境梯度推进。
senses.why: Para- 'beside' plus patria marks neighbouring ranges: the populations touch at a border but do not freely mix.
senses.whyCN: para-「旁侧」加 patria 表示相邻分布区：群体在边界相接，却不自由混合。

senses.title: Reproductive isolation as the decisive step
senses.titleCN: 生殖隔离作为决定性一步
senses.definition: the point at which two diverging forms can no longer interbreed successfully, so the split is complete
senses.definitionCN: 两个分化中的类型不再能成功互交、分化由此完成的那个节点
senses.example: Speciation is complete only when the two forms no longer interbreed.
senses.exampleCN: 只有当两个类型不再互交时，物种形成才算完成。
senses.why: A species is a breeding community, so the process is finished when that community has become two; isolation is the test, not the scenery.
senses.whyCN: 物种就是一个繁殖共同体，因此当这个共同体变成两个时过程即告完成；生殖隔离是判据，而不是背景。

senses.title: Polyploid speciation in a single generation
senses.titleCN: 多倍体物种形成：一代之内完成
senses.definition: the origin of a new species through a change in chromosome number, often instant and common in plants
senses.definitionCN: 通过染色体数目变化产生新物种，常在一代之内完成，在植物中很常见
senses.example: Polyploid speciation produced a fertile hybrid within a single generation.
senses.exampleCN: 多倍体物种形成在一代之内就产生了可育的杂种。
senses.why: When chromosome doubling makes a hybrid fertile with its own kind but not with its parents, the new species appears at once rather than gradually.
senses.whyCN: 当染色体加倍使杂种能与同类可育、却不能与亲本可育时，新物种立刻出现，而非逐渐形成。

senses.title: Speciation rate in macroevolution
senses.titleCN: 宏观演化中的物种形成速率
senses.definition: the frequency with which new species arise in a lineage over geological time, often measured as events per million years
senses.definitionCN: 某一谱系在地质时间尺度上新物种产生的频率，常以每百万年的事件数计
senses.example: The fossil record shows bursts of speciation after each mass extinction.
senses.exampleCN: 化石记录显示，每次大灭绝之后都出现物种形成的爆发。
senses.why: Once the process is dated in the rock record, speciation becomes a rate: how many splits per unit time a clade produces.
senses.whyCN: 当这一过程能在岩石记录中定年时，物种形成就变成了速率：一个支系在单位时间内产生多少次分裂。

senses.title: Speciation observed in the laboratory
senses.titleCN: 实验室中观测到的物种形成
senses.definition: the experimental production of reproductive isolation between laboratory populations, as in long-running selection lines
senses.definitionCN: 在实验条件下使实验室群体之间产生生殖隔离，例如长期选择实验中的品系
senses.example: Speciation in the laboratory was documented when two fly lines stopped mating.
senses.exampleCN: 当两个果蝇品系不再交配时，实验室中的物种形成得到了记录。
senses.why: Experimental evolution makes the process observable within a career: the split is measured as a mating preference rather than inferred from fossils.
senses.whyCN: 实验演化使这一过程在一个人一生之内可被观察：分裂以交配偏好的形式测量，而不必从化石推断。

intro.en: Speciation is a nineteenth-century noun made from species, the Latin word for 'kind, appearance', plus the process suffix -ation. The date is approximate, and the deepest Indo-European layer is a reconstruction.
intro.cn: speciation 是 19 世纪由 species（拉丁语「种类、外观」）加过程后缀 -ation 构成的名词。年代为约数，最深层印欧语层属于重构。

items.en: Species in Latin meant 'sight, appearance, form, kind'. It was a fifth-declension noun, and its plural was also species.
items.cn: 拉丁语 species 意为「视觉、外观、形态、种类」，是第五变格法名词，复数形式同样是 species。

items.en: The noun rests on specere 'to look, to see'; the same root gives specimen, spectacle and spectrum.
items.cn: 该名词基于 specere「看、观看」；同一词根还给出 specimen、spectacle 与 spectrum。

items.en: The Latin suffix -atio(n)- named an action or its result; English -ation turned species into the name of a process rather than a category.
items.cn: 拉丁后缀 -atio(n)- 表示动作或其结果；英语 -ation 把 species 由类别名称变成过程名称。

items.en: The noun speciation is recorded in English from the mid-nineteenth century, when evolutionary biology needed a word for the origin of species.
items.cn: 名词 speciation 于 19 世纪中叶见于英语，当时演化生物学正需要一个词来指物种的起源。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word was divided by geography into allopatric, sympatric and parapatric modes, each with its own prefix.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个词按地理条件被分为异域、同域与邻域三种模式，每种都带各自的前缀。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first citation of speciation is not fixed here, and the pre-Latin origin of specere is a reconstruction rather than an attested form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：speciation 最早书证的确切年份此处无法确定；specere 在拉丁语之前的来源属重构形式，而非有据可查的形式。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the Latin spec- stock that look alike; group two holds processes that are close in meaning but not identical.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁 spec- 词干、外形相近的词；第二组是意思接近但并不相同的各种过程。

entries.definition: The category itself, whose plural is unchanged. Speciation is the process by which a new species comes into being.
entries.definitionCN: 物种这一范畴本身，复数形式不变。speciation 则是新物种产生的过程。

entries.definition: A single sample used for study, from the same specere 'to look'. It names an object, not a process.
entries.definitionCN: 供研究用的单个样本，同出 specere「看」。它指实物，不指过程。

entries.definition: A detailed statement of requirements, from species in its 'kind' sense plus facere 'to make'. It has no evolutionary meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 对要求的详细说明，由 species 的「种类」义加 facere「做」构成，没有演化含义。

entries.definition: The development of a form fitted to a particular function, from specialis 'individual, particular'. It is not speciation.
entries.definitionCN: 发展出适应特定功能的形式，来自 specialis「个别的、特定的」，并非物种形成。

entries.definition: Change in heritable traits over generations. Speciation is one kind of evolution, not its synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 可遗传性状在世代间的变化。物种形成是演化的一种，并非其同义词。

entries.definition: The separation of lineages from a common ancestor; it may occur without full reproductive isolation.
entries.definitionCN: 谱系从共同祖先分开；这种分开未必达到完全的生殖隔离。

entries.definition: The rapid diversification of one lineage into many species filling different niches. It is a pattern made of many speciation events.
entries.definitionCN: 一个谱系迅速分化为许多占据不同生态位的物种；它是由多次物种形成构成的格局。

entries.definition: Crossing between distinct taxa, which can sometimes create a new species but is the opposite direction of gene flow.
entries.definitionCN: 不同类群间的杂交，有时能产生新物种，但基因流方向与分化相反。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: species 'kind' + -ation 'process': speciation is literally the process of a new kind appearing.
normal.cn: species「种类」+ -ation「过程」：speciation 字面就是新种类出现的过程。

normal.en: The three geographical modes carry their own prefixes: allo- other land, sym- same land, para- beside land.
normal.cn: 三种地理模式各带前缀：allo- 别的土地、sym- 同一土地、para- 旁侧土地。

normal.en: Reproductive isolation is the finishing line; a species is a breeding community, so two communities mean two species.
normal.cn: 生殖隔离是终点线；物种是繁殖共同体，因此两个共同体就意味着两个物种。

normal.en: Polyploidy can finish the job in one generation, which is why speciation is often instant in plants.
normal.cn: 多倍体可以在一代之内完成这件事，这就是植物中物种形成常常是瞬间发生的原因。

normal.en: Speciation rate is the fossil-record version of the word: splits per million years.
normal.cn: 物种形成速率是这个词在化石记录中的形态：每百万年发生多少次分裂。

abstract.en: Picture a rope fraying into two cords that can no longer be spliced back together.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子分成两股，再也无法重新编回一根。

abstract.en: Picture two dialects drifting apart until neither speaker understands the other.
abstract.cn: 想象两种方言渐行渐远，直到双方都听不懂对方。

abstract.en: Picture a broken bridge between two islands: the same boats can no longer reach either shore.
abstract.cn: 想象两座岛之间的桥断了：同一批船再也到不了对岸。

examples.en: Speciation in island birds followed each colonization of an empty archipelago.
examples.cn: 岛屿鸟类的物种形成在每一次登上空群岛之后发生。

examples.en: The two orchids count as one species until the day their pollinators stop sharing.
examples.cn: 这两种兰花仍算一个物种，直到它们的传粉者不再共享的那一天。

examples.en: Museum collections supply the dates used to estimate speciation rates.
examples.cn: 博物馆藏品提供了估算物种形成速率所需的年代数据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「specia」——一个「种」加一个「过程」，新种就这样生出来 → speciation 物种形成

root: 拉丁 species「种类、外观」+ -ation「过程」；species 出自 specere「看、观看」，同根词有 specimen、spectacle、spectrum。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of speciation all name one event seen at different scales: a breeding community splits, and the split can be caused by a river, by a host shift, by doubled chromosomes, by geological time or by a laboratory cage.
sensesIntro.cn: speciation 的八个义项都指同一事件在不同尺度上的呈现：一个繁殖共同体分裂，而分裂的起因可以是河流、寄主转换、染色体加倍、地质时间或实验室的笼子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one breeding community becoming two that no longer exchange members.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个繁殖共同体变成两个，彼此不再交换成员。

branches.en: THE WHOLE PROCESS: speciation is the name of the split itself, seen from start to finish.
branches.cn: 整个过程：speciation 就是分裂本身的名称，从开头看到结尾。

branches.en: WHERE IT HAPPENS: other land, same land and neighbouring land give the three geographical modes.
branches.cn: 发生在哪里：别的土地、同一土地、相邻土地给出三种地理模式。

branches.en: THE TEST: the split counts as complete only when interbreeding fails.
branches.cn: 判据：只有互交失败时，分裂才算完成。

branches.en: SUDDEN MODE: doubled chromosomes can finish the split within one generation.
branches.cn: 突变模式：染色体加倍能在一代之内完成分裂。

branches.en: MEASURED IN TIME: fossils give a rate per million years, cages give a rate per career.
branches.cn: 在时间中测量：化石给出每百万年的速率，笼子给出每人一生的速率。

intro.en: Speciation is transparent once species and -ation are separated: one Latin noun of kind, one Latin suffix of process.
intro.cn: 只要把 species 与 -ation 分开，speciation 就一目了然：一个表示种类的拉丁名词，一个表示过程的拉丁后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin species gives the English family species, specious and speciose; specere adds specimen, spectacle, spectrum and inspect.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 species 衍生英语的 species、specious 与 speciose；specere 另给出 specimen、spectacle、spectrum 与 inspect。

items.example: Species is both singular and plural in English.
items.exampleCN: species 在英语中单复数同形。

items.example: The root names the visible mark that sorts one kind from another.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指用来区分种类的可见标记。

items.example: Island flies speciate on each newly raised ridge.
items.exampleCN: 岛上的果蝇在每一道新升起的山脊上形成新种。

items.example: The suffix turns a category into an event.
items.exampleCN: 该后缀把类别变成事件。

items.example: Speciation is measured as a rate in the fossil record.
items.exampleCN: 物种形成在化石记录中以速率计量。

items.example: Subspeciation preceded full isolation in the northern range.
items.exampleCN: 在北部分布区，亚种分化先于完全隔离。

items.example: The speciose genus fills every damp hollow.
items.exampleCN: 这个多物种的属填满了每一处潮湿洼地。

items.example: Speciational bursts followed the lake's formation.
items.exampleCN: 物种形成的爆发随湖泊形成而来。

definition_zh: 物种；种；种类；（神学）圣餐的外观
definition_en: a group of living things that share inherited features and can breed with one another, or a kind of thing in general
core_image: 一群能互相交配、留下后代的个体，被一条看不见的界线围在同一处
scene: 护林员在同一条山谷里记录到三种不同的蛾类，每一种都只在特定的海拔带活动。 In one valley the rangers recorded three different moth species, each restricted to its own band of elevation.
sceneCN: 这里 species 是「物种」（第 1 个义项：生物分类的基本单位）；句意：护林员在同一条山谷里记录到三种不同的蛾类，每一种都只在特定的海拔带活动。

pos.zh: 物种；种（单复数同形）；种类；（神学）圣餐的外观

derivatives.zh: 特定的；具体的（同出 species 词根）
似是而非的；外观好看而实质可疑的

senses.title: The basic unit of biological classification
senses.definition: the rank below genus in biological classification, made up of populations that share a common inheritance
senses.definitionCN: 生物分类中位于属之下的等级，由具有共同遗传特征的群体构成
senses.example: The rangers logged three moth species in the same valley.
senses.exampleCN: 护林员在同一条山谷里记录了三种蛾。
senses.why: Species is the Latin word for 'appearance, kind'; taxonomy took that everyday noun and made it the unit against which all other ranks are measured.
senses.whyCN: species 本是拉丁语「外观、种类」；分类学把这个日常名词变成了衡量其他所有阶元的单位。

senses.title: A community that interbreeds
senses.titleCN: 能互相交配的繁殖共同体
senses.definition: the biological species concept: a group whose members can interbreed and produce fertile offspring but cannot do so with outsiders
senses.definitionCN: 生物学物种概念：成员能互交并产生可育后代、却无法与外部成员如此繁殖的群体
senses.example: A species is defined by interbreeding, not by resemblance alone.
senses.exampleCN: 物种是由能否互交来定义的，而不只是由相似程度来定义。
senses.why: The definition is a test rather than a picture: two forms may look alike and still fail the breeding test, which is why the word can be argued over.
senses.whyCN: 这个定义是判据而不是图像：两个类型可以长得很像却过不了繁殖这一关，这正是这个词常被争论的原因。

senses.title: Singular and plural in one form
senses.definition: the same written form for one species and for several, a surviving Latin fifth-declension plural
senses.definitionCN: 一个物种与多个物种使用同一书写形式，这是拉丁第五变格法复数留下的痕迹
senses.example: Three species were found, and one species was new to the island.
senses.exampleCN: 发现了三个物种，其中一个在该岛是首次记录。
senses.why: Latin species was already both singular and plural, and English kept the form unchanged, so number must be read from the verb or the number word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 species 本就单复数同形，英语保留了这一形式，因此单复数只能从动词或数量词读出。

senses.title: A kind or sort in ordinary use
senses.definition: a kind of thing, often in the phrase a species of, where no biological meaning is involved
senses.definitionCN: 某一种事物，常用于表示「一种……」的结构，与生物学无关
senses.example: A species of stubbornness kept him at the bench long after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 一种固执让他过了午夜仍守在实验台前。
senses.why: The everyday sense keeps the old Latin breadth: species can name any kind at all, and biology later narrowed one branch of it.
senses.whyCN: 日常义保留了拉丁语原有的宽度：species 可以指任何种类，生物学后来只收窄了其中一支。

senses.title: The logical species under a genus
senses.definition: in logic, a subordinate class contained within a wider class, the species under its genus
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑学中包在更大类别之内的下级类别，即其属之下的种
senses.example: In the old logic, humanity is a species and animal is its genus.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧逻辑中，「人」是一个种，而「动物」是它的属。
senses.why: Logic used species and genus long before biology: the pair named a relation of containment, and Linnaeus simply borrowed that ladder for living things.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学远在生物学之前就使用 species 与 genus：这对词表示包含关系，林奈只是把这架梯子借来安放生物。

senses.title: A unit for counting biodiversity
senses.titleCN: 生物多样性的计数单位
senses.definition: the unit in which richness is counted, as in the number of species on an island or in a forest plot
senses.definitionCN: 衡量丰富度的单位，如一座岛或一块林地中的物种数
senses.example: The survey counted 214 species in a single hectare of forest.
senses.exampleCN: 这次调查在一公顷森林中就数到 214 个物种。
senses.why: Conservation needs a countable unit, and the species supplies it: richness is simply how many of these units are present.
senses.whyCN: 保护工作需要可计数的单位，而物种提供了它：丰富度就是这种单位出现了多少个。

senses.title: A mineral or chemical species
senses.definition: a distinct mineral or chemical form defined by composition and structure, as in mineral species
senses.definitionCN: 由成分与结构定义的独立矿物或化学形态，如矿物种
senses.example: The geologist identified the mineral species from its crystal lattice.
senses.exampleCN: 地质学家根据晶格确定了这个矿物种。
senses.why: The word's 'distinct kind' sense was borrowed by chemistry and mineralogy, where a species is a kind fixed by composition rather than by breeding.
senses.whyCN: 这个词「独立种类」的意思被化学与矿物学借用，在那里物种由成分而非繁殖来界定。

senses.title: The outward forms in Eucharistic theology
senses.definition: in Christian theology, the outward appearances of bread and wine that remain after consecration
senses.definitionCN: 基督教神学中，祝圣之后仍存留的饼与酒的外部形态
senses.example: Theologians speak of the species of bread and wine, not of their substance.
senses.exampleCN: 神学家说的是饼与酒的外观，而不是它们的实体。
senses.why: This is the oldest Latin sense, 'appearance', surviving in a technical corner: what the senses perceive is the species, while the substance is held to be changed.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的拉丁义「外观」在一个术语角落里的存留：感官所感知的是外观，而实体被认为已经改变。

senses.title: Species as a category in philosophy of biology
senses.titleCN: 生物学哲学中的「物种范畴」
senses.definition: the unit whose ontological status is debated, whether a natural kind, a population or a historical individual
senses.definitionCN: 其本体地位仍有争论的单位：究竟为自然种类、群体还是历史个体
senses.example: Philosophers ask whether a species is a class or an individual history.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家追问：物种究竟是一个类，还是一段个体历史。
senses.why: Because the word names both a category and a concrete lineage, philosophers can ask what kind of thing it is, a question the biological definition alone does not settle.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个词既指范畴又指具体谱系，哲学家可以追问它究竟是哪一类东西，而单靠生物学定义并不能解决这个问题。

intro.en: Species is a Latin noun taken into English unchanged in form and meaning; its plural is the same word. Dates are approximate, and the Indo-European layer is reconstructed.
intro.cn: species 是原形原义进入英语的拉丁名词，复数形式相同。年代为约数，印欧语层属重构。

items.en: Species meant 'a sight, a look, an appearance', and from that 'a form or kind'. It belonged to the fifth declension.
items.cn: species 意为「所见、外观」，由此引申为「形态、种类」，属第五变格法。

items.en: The noun derives from specere 'to look, see'; the same root yields specimen, spectacle, spectrum and inspect.
items.cn: 该名词出自 specere「看、观看」；同根词有 specimen、spectacle、spectrum、inspect。

items.en: Medieval logic used species for a class contained under a genus, a relation of containment rather than of breeding.
items.cn: 中世纪逻辑学用 species 指包含在属之下的类，这是一种包含关系，而非繁殖关系。

items.en: Linnaeus fixed species as the basic rank of his system in the eighteenth century and placed it under genus in the binomial name.
items.cn: 林奈在 18 世纪把 species 定为系统的基本阶元，并在双名法中把它置于属名之下。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word was sharpened into a breeding community, so that species became a testable claim rather than a resemblance.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个词被明确为繁殖共同体，species 于是成为可检验的判断，而不再只是相似程度。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the precise first English citation is not fixed here, and the pre-Latin origin of specere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：species 最早的英语书证此处无法确定；specere 在拉丁语之前的来源属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates forms built on the Latin spec- stock; group two places species among the ranks and processes around it.
note.cn: 第一组区分同出拉丁 spec- 词干的各形；第二组把 species 放回它周围的阶元与过程。

entries.definition: A single individual or sample kept for study. It is one object, while species is a whole kind.
entries.definitionCN: 留作研究的单个个体或样本。它是一个物件，而 species 是整个种类。

entries.definition: Apparently good or true but actually not, from the 'appearance' sense of species. It is an adjective, not a rank.
entries.definitionCN: 看似良好或真实而实际不然，出自 species 的「外观」义。它是形容词，不是阶元。

entries.definition: Clearly defined or peculiar to one thing, from specialis. It answers 'which one', while species answers 'what kind'.
entries.definitionCN: 明确界定的或某一事物特有的，出自 specialis。它回答「哪一个」，species 回答「哪一类」。

entries.definition: Distinct from the ordinary, from specialis 'individual, particular'. The link to species is through 'a particular appearance'.
entries.definitionCN: 与寻常不同的，出自 specialis「个别的、特定的」。与 species 的联系经由「特定外观」这一层。

entries.definition: A geographically or morphologically distinct subdivision of a species, written as a trinomial.
entries.definitionCN: 物种之下在地理或形态上有所区别的细分，用三名法书写。

entries.definition: The rank above species, grouping species that share a common ancestor and structure.
entries.definitionCN: species 之上的阶元，把共享祖先与结构的物种聚在一起。

entries.definition: A group of individuals of one species living in one area and interbreeding. It is a part of a species, not the rank itself.
entries.definitionCN: 同一物种在同一地区生活并互交的一群个体；它是物种的一部分，而非阶元本身。

entries.definition: A genetically distinct line within a species, used in laboratories and breeding. It is finer than a subspecies.
entries.definitionCN: 物种内遗传上独立的品系，用于实验室与育种；比亚种更细。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: species comes from specere 'to look': a species was first an appearance, then a kind that looks the same.
normal.cn: species 出自 specere「看」：物种最初是一种外观，后来指外观一致的种类。

normal.en: The plural does not change: three species, one species, and the verb tells you which.
normal.cn: 复数形式不变：三个物种与一个物种都写作同一个形式，单复数由动词告知。

normal.en: The binomial name puts genus first and species second, as in Panthera leo.
normal.cn: 双名法把属名在前、种名在后，如 Panthera leo。

normal.en: The Endangered Species Act is the best-known legal use of the word as a countable unit.
normal.cn: 《濒危物种法》是这个词作为可计数单位最著名的法律用法。

normal.en: Logic used species under genus long before biology borrowed the ladder.
normal.cn: 逻辑学早在生物学借用这架梯子之前就使用「属下的种」。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd sorted by a single question: can these two have young together?
abstract.cn: 想象一群人被一个问题筛选：这两个能否共同留下后代？

abstract.en: Picture a library where one label fits a whole shelf and the same label also fits a single book.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，一个标签既贴满一整架，也贴在一本书上。

abstract.en: Picture an old coin still used in a corner of commerce, its face worn but its value unchanged.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚旧硬币仍在某个商业角落流通，表面磨旧而价值不变。

examples.en: The lake holds more species than any other body of fresh water in the region.
examples.cn: 这个湖里的物种数多于该地区任何其他淡水水体。

examples.en: A species of quiet confidence spread through the laboratory after the result held.
examples.cn: 结果依然成立之后，一种平静的自信在实验室里传开。

examples.en: The mineral species was named for the valley where it was first found.
examples.cn: 这个矿物种以首次发现它的山谷命名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「specy 像一片」——长得一样、能一起生育的一群 → species 物种

root: 拉丁 species「外观、种类」，出自 specere「看、观看」；单复数同形，属第五变格法。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of species move from the taxonomic unit outward to the breeding community, the unchanged plural, the everyday kind, the logical class, the biodiversity count, the mineral kind, the theological appearance and finally the philosophical question of what a species is.
sensesIntro.cn: species 的九个义项从分类单位向外展开：繁殖共同体、单复数同形、日常种类、逻辑类别、生物多样性计数、矿物种类、神学外观，最后是「物种究竟是什么」的哲学追问。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a visible kind circled by an invisible breeding line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个可见的种类被一条看不见的繁殖界线围住。

branches.en: THE UNIT AND ITS TEST: the rank is defined by interbreeding, so resemblance alone cannot make a species.
branches.cn: 单位与判据：这个阶元由互交定义，单凭相似不能构成物种。

branches.en: THE FORM: Latin left the plural unchanged, so number lives in the syntax.
branches.cn: 形式：拉丁语留下同形复数，单复数因此藏在句法里。

branches.en: THE OLD BREADTH: everyday 'a species of' and the logical species under a genus both keep the pre-biological meaning.
branches.cn: 古老的宽度：日常的「一种」与逻辑学中属下的种都保留了生物学之前的意义。

branches.en: THE COUNT AND THE MINERAL: the word serves as a countable unit in ecology and as a fixed kind in mineralogy.
branches.cn: 计数与矿物：这个词在生态学中是计数单位，在矿物学中是固定的种类。

branches.en: APPEARANCE AND ONTOLOGY: the oldest sense survives in theology, while philosophy asks what kind of thing a species is.
branches.cn: 外观与本体：最古老的义在神学中存留，哲学则追问物种是哪一类存在。

intro.en: Species is one Latin noun with a long afterlife: appearance, kind, logical class, biological rank and theological form all sit in the same word.
intro.cn: species 是一个有很长后续生命的拉丁名词：外观、种类、逻辑类别、生物阶元与神学形态都栖在同一个词里。

latinIntro.en: Latin species yields English species, special, specific, specious and speciose; specere yields specimen, spectacle, spectrum and inspect.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 species 衍生英语 species、special、specific、specious、speciose；specere 衍生 specimen、spectacle、spectrum、inspect。

items.example: Species serves as both singular and plural.
items.exampleCN: species 单复数同形。

items.example: The root names what is seen and therefore what is recognized.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指所见之物，因而指被识别出的东西。

items.example: Specialis narrows the kind to one case.
items.exampleCN: specialis 把种类收窄到某一个情形。

items.example: Subspecies names a rank below the basic unit.
items.exampleCN: subspecies 指基本单位之下的阶元。

items.example: Speciation is the process, species the result.
items.exampleCN: speciation 是过程，species 是结果。

items.example: A speciose forest rewards a slow walk.
items.exampleCN: 物种丰富的森林值得慢慢走。

items.example: The specious argument survived only one question.
items.exampleCN: 这个似是而非的论点只经住了一个追问。

items.example: A specific answer names one case.
items.exampleCN: 明确的回答会点出某一个情形。

definition_zh: 亚种；种以下的分类等级
definition_en: a group of populations within a species that differ from other populations, usually in geography or form
core_image: 同一片大陆上被山脉隔开的两群同类，毛色深浅不同，却仍能互交
scene: 博物馆把来自两座相隔很远的岛屿的甲虫标本定为同一物种下的两个不同亚种。 The museum assigned beetle specimens from two distant islands to two different subspecies of the same species.
sceneCN: 这里 subspecies 是「亚种」（第 1 个义项：种之下的分类等级）；句意：博物馆把来自两座相隔很远岛屿的甲虫标本，定为同一物种下的两个不同亚种。

pos.zh: 亚种（单复数同形，略作 subsp. 或 ssp.）

derivatives.zh: 变种（植物分类中低于亚种的等级）
变型（植物分类中的最低等级）

senses.title: A rank below species
senses.definition: the taxonomic rank immediately below species, grouping populations that share a distinct set of features
senses.definitionCN: 紧接在物种之下的分类阶元，把具有一组独特性状的群体聚合起来
senses.example: The museum assigned the two island beetles to different subspecies.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆把两座岛上的甲虫定为不同的亚种。
senses.why: Sub- 'under' plus species makes the rank literal: the same kind, divided one step further down.
senses.whyCN: sub-「在下」加 species 把阶元关系写得很直白：同一个种，再往下分一级。

senses.title: A geographical race
senses.definition: a set of populations separated by geography that have come to differ in colour, size or behaviour while remaining interfertile
senses.definitionCN: 因地理分隔而在毛色、体型或行为上出现差异、却仍能互交的群体
senses.example: The northern subspecies is darker and slightly smaller.
senses.exampleCN: 北方的亚种颜色更深，体型略小。
senses.why: Most subspecies begin as geography: a barrier stops gene flow long enough for local features to accumulate, but not long enough to block breeding.
senses.whyCN: 多数亚种起于地理：屏障阻断基因流的时间足以让地方特征积累，却还不足以阻断繁殖。

senses.title: The trinomial name
senses.definition: the three-part scientific name that adds a subspecies epithet to the binomial, as in Homo sapiens sapiens
senses.definitionCN: 在双名之后再加一个亚种加词的三段式学名，如智人的指名亚种
senses.example: The trinomial name repeats the species epithet for the nominate subspecies.
senses.exampleCN: 指名亚种的名称会把种加词重复一遍。
senses.why: Because a subspecies sits below a species, its name needs one more slot; the trinomial is that slot, and it is written in italics with the rank not capitalized.
senses.whyCN: 由于亚种位于种之下，其名称需要多一个位置；三名法就是那个位置，书写时用斜体且亚种加词不大写。

senses.title: Nomenclatural rules and abbreviations
senses.definition: the set of rules that govern valid subspecies names, together with the abbreviations subsp. and ssp. used in catalogs
senses.definitionCN: 管理亚种名称有效性的规则，以及标本目录中使用的缩写 subsp. 与 ssp.
senses.example: The label reads subsp. borealis, following the code.
senses.exampleCN: 标签按法规写作 subsp. borealis。
senses.why: Codes exist so that a name means the same thing in every collection; the abbreviation marks the rank without spelling it out, which saves space on a label.
senses.whyCN: 法规的存在是为了让一个名称在每一份收藏中都指同一事物；缩写在不写出全称的情况下标出阶元，可节省标签空间。

senses.title: Plural identical to singular
senses.definition: the form subspecies used for both one and several, following the Latin pattern of species
senses.definitionCN: 一个与多个都写作 subspecies，沿用 species 的拉丁模式
senses.example: Two subspecies were recognized, and one subspecies was newly described.
senses.exampleCN: 识别出两个亚种，其中一个为新描述。
senses.why: Latin species had an unchanging plural, and the compound keeps it: only the verb or a numeral shows whether the word is singular.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 species 的复数不变，这个复合词沿用了这一点：只有动词或数词能表明该词是单数还是复数。

senses.title: Subspecies and variety in botany
senses.titleCN: 植物学中亚种与变种的分别
senses.definition: in botanical nomenclature, a rank that ranks above variety and below species, used for geographically distinct wild populations
senses.definitionCN: 植物命名法中位于变种之上、物种之下、用于地理上独立的野生群体的等级
senses.example: Botanists treat the coastal form as a subspecies, not a variety.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学家把海岸类型处理为亚种，而不是变种。
senses.why: Botany needed finer steps than zoology, so it placed variety and forma below subspecies; the two words are not interchangeable.
senses.whyCN: 植物学需要比动物学更细的台阶，于是在亚种之下再设变种与变型；这两个词不能互换。

senses.title: A unit in conservation planning
senses.definition: a population unit recognized in conservation because its distinct traits would be lost if it disappeared
senses.definitionCN: 因其独特性状一旦消失就会丧失、而在保护工作中被承认的群体单元
senses.example: Managers list the island subspecies as a priority for captive breeding.
senses.exampleCN: 管理者把这个岛屿亚种列为圈养繁殖的优先对象。
senses.why: Conservation works with units it can act on; a named subspecies gives a legal and practical handle even when the biological status is debated.
senses.whyCN: 保护工作需要可施加行动的单元；即使生物学地位仍有争议，一个有名称的亚种也提供了法律与实践上的抓手。

senses.title: Subspecies in microbiology
senses.definition: a formal rank used for bacterial strains that differ in antigenic or biochemical characters within one species
senses.definitionCN: 用于同一物种内抗原或生化性状不同的菌株的正式等级
senses.example: The culture was classified as a subspecies of the common gut bacterium.
senses.exampleCN: 该培养物被定为常见肠道细菌的一个亚种。
senses.why: Microbiology adopted the rank because bacterial species can be very broad; subspecies gives a legal name to a recognizable strain without raising it to species.
senses.whyCN: 微生物学采用这个等级，因为细菌的种可以定得很宽；亚种给了可辨识菌株一个正式名称，而无需把它提升为种。

senses.title: The rank as a matter of judgement
senses.titleCN: 作为判断问题的亚种划分
senses.definition: a classification that depends on how much difference taxonomists decide is enough, and therefore often revised
senses.definitionCN: 取决于分类学家认定差异足够大与否、因而常被修订的分类处理
senses.example: The two subspecies were later merged when the boundary proved continuous.
senses.exampleCN: 当界线被证明是连续的，这两个亚种后来被合并。
senses.why: Subspecies is the rank most exposed to disagreement, since the line between a local form and a full species is drawn by judgement rather than by a single test.
senses.whyCN: 亚种是最容易引起分歧的阶元，因为地方类型与完整物种之间的界线靠判断划定，而不是靠单一判据。

intro.en: Subspecies is a modern scientific compound: Latin sub- 'under' fastened to species. It was coined for taxonomy rather than inherited from Latin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: subspecies 是近代科学复合词：拉丁前缀 sub-「在下」加 species，为分类学而造，并非从拉丁语整体继承。年代为约数。

items.en: Sub- meant 'under, below' and was already productive in Latin compounds such as subicere and substructio.
items.cn: sub- 意为「在下、低于」，在拉丁复合词中已很能产，如 subicere 与 substructio。

items.en: Species meant 'appearance, kind' and served as the basic logical class before it became a biological rank.
items.cn: species 意为「外观、种类」，在成为生物阶元之前是基本的逻辑类别。

items.en: As ranks multiplied, naturalists needed a step between the broad species of the day and the local form, and the compound was available.
items.cn: 随着阶元增多，博物学者需要在当时较宽的种与地方类型之间加一级，而这个复合形式正好可用。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century nomenclature codes fixed the trinomial and the abbreviations subsp. and ssp.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪的命名法规确定了三名法以及 subsp.、ssp. 两种缩写。

items.en: Molecular data have forced many subspecies to be merged or raised, so the rank is now more often a provisional judgement than a settled fact.
items.cn: 分子数据迫使许多亚种被合并或提升，因此这个阶元如今更像临时判断，而非定论。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first use of subspecies as a formal rank is not fixed here, and no classical Latin noun subspecies is attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：subspecies 作为正式阶元的最早使用年份此处无法确定；古典拉丁语中并无 subspecies 这一名词。

note.en: Group one separates ranks and names that sit near subspecies; group two compares the words for local forms at different depths.
note.cn: 第一组区分与亚种相邻的阶元与名称；第二组比较不同深度的「地方类型」用词。

entries.definition: The basic rank itself: one step up from subspecies, and the unit that the trinomial's second word names.
entries.definitionCN: 基本阶元本身：比亚种高一级，也是三名法中第二个词所命名的单位。

entries.definition: Relating to a subspecies, as in subspecific epithet. It is the adjective, while subspecies is the rank noun.
entries.definitionCN: 与亚种有关的，如亚种加词。它是形容词，subspecies 是阶元名词。

entries.definition: A group of closely related species treated together, the opposite direction from subspecies.
entries.definitionCN: 把若干近缘物种合并看待的类群，方向与亚种相反。

entries.definition: A mathematical space contained in another space. Sub- is shared, but species is not the source; it is built on space.
entries.definitionCN: 包含于另一空间的数学空间。共用了 sub-，但词源不是 species，而是建立在 space 之上。

entries.definition: In botany, a rank below subspecies for a minor wild variant; in everyday use, simply a sort or kind.
entries.definitionCN: 植物学中位于亚种之下、用于细微野生变异的等级；日常则泛指种类。

entries.definition: A loosely used term for a geographically distinct breeding group; it has no fixed rank in the codes.
entries.definitionCN: 对地理上独立的繁殖群体的宽松称呼；在命名法规中没有固定阶元。

entries.definition: A genetically distinct line maintained in the laboratory or in breeding, finer and less formal than a subspecies.
entries.definitionCN: 实验室或育种中保持的遗传独立品系，比亚种更细、更不正式。

entries.definition: In botany, forma, a minor morphological variant below variety; the smallest recognized step.
entries.definitionCN: 植物学中的变型，位于变种之下、最小的可识别台阶。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: sub- 'under' plus species: one step below the basic rank.
normal.cn: sub-「在下」加 species：基本阶元之下的一级。

normal.en: The trinomial adds a third word: genus, species, subspecies.
normal.cn: 三名法再加一个词：属名、种名、亚种名。

normal.en: The nomination subspecies repeats the species epithet, which makes it easy to spot in a name.
normal.cn: 指名亚种会重复种加词，因此在名称里一眼可辨。

normal.en: Botany puts variety and forma below subspecies, so the ranks are ordered rather than interchangeable.
normal.cn: 植物学把变种与变型放在亚种之下，因此这些阶元有先后，不能互换。

normal.en: Labels abbreviate the rank as subsp. or ssp. to save space.
normal.cn: 标签把阶元缩写成 subsp. 或 ssp. 以节省空间。

abstract.en: Picture a country with provinces: still one country, but each province has its own flag.
abstract.cn: 想象一个有省份的国家：仍是一个国家，但每省有自己的旗。

abstract.en: Picture two editions of one book, differing in a chapter or two but readable as the same work.
abstract.cn: 想象同一本书的两个版本，相差一两章，却仍可读作同一部作品。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn on a map by a committee, revised at the next meeting.
abstract.cn: 想象一条由委员会在地图上划出的线，下次会议又被修订。

examples.en: The desert subspecies nests earlier than the coastal one.
examples.cn: 沙漠亚种比海岸亚种更早筑巢。

examples.en: Codes require the subspecies epithet to be lower-case even when it honours a place.
examples.cn: 法规要求亚种加词即使纪念地名也用小写。

examples.en: A recent review sank three subspecies into one on genetic evidence.
examples.cn: 最近一篇综述依据遗传证据把三个亚种合并为一个。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sub 在下 + species 物种」——物种底下的那一层 → subspecies 亚种

root: 拉丁 sub-「在下」+ species「物种」；近代分类学为表示种下阶元而造的复合词，古典拉丁语无此名词。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of subspecies follow the rank from its formal position downward: a step below species, a geographic race, a three-word name, a set of naming rules, an unchanging plural, a botanical neighbour, a conservation unit, a microbiological label and finally a judgement that keeps being revised.
sensesIntro.cn: subspecies 的九个义项沿着这个阶元向下展开：种下的一级、地理宗、三名式名称、命名规则、不变的复数、植物学中的邻级、保护单元、微生物学标签，最后是一个不断被修订的判断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one kind divided by a map line that is real enough to name but not deep enough to split.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个种类被一条地图上的线分开，足以命名，却不足以分裂。

branches.en: THE RANK AND ITS ORIGIN: a step below species, usually produced by geography.
branches.cn: 阶元与来源：种下的一级，通常由地理分隔产生。

branches.en: THE NAME: three words, a code of rules, and a plural that never changes form.
branches.cn: 名称：三个词、一套规则、一个永不改变形式的复数。

branches.en: BOTANICAL ORDER: variety and forma sit still lower, so the ranks form a ladder.
branches.cn: 植物学的次序：变种与变型还在更低处，阶元因此形成梯子。

branches.en: APPLIED USES: conservation acts on the named unit, microbiology uses it for strains.
branches.cn: 应用：保护工作作用于有名称的单元，微生物学用它标记菌株。

branches.en: THE JUDGEMENT: how much difference is enough is decided, not measured.
branches.cn: 判断：差异要多大才算够，是决定的，不是测出来的。

intro.en: Subspecies is built from two Latin pieces but is itself a modern scientific word; the pieces are transparent even though the compound is recent.
intro.cn: subspecies 由两个拉丁成分构成，但本身是近代科学词；复合词虽新，成分却透明。

latinIntro.en: Latin sub- yields submarine, subsoil and subordinate; species yields species, subspecies and speciation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sub- 衍生 submarine、subsoil、subordinate；species 衍生 species、subspecies、speciation。

items.example: Sub- places the rank one step lower.
items.exampleCN: sub- 把这个阶元放到低一级的位置。

items.example: Species supplies the rank that is being divided.
items.exampleCN: species 提供被再分的那个阶元。

items.example: The island form is treated as a subspecies.
items.exampleCN: 岛上的类型被处理为亚种。

items.example: A subspecific name follows the trinomial.
items.exampleCN: 亚种名按三名法书写。

items.example: The label reads subsp. borealis.
items.exampleCN: 标签写作 subsp. borealis。

items.example: Older catalogs prefer ssp. to subsp.
items.exampleCN: 较老的目录更常用 ssp. 而非 subsp.。

items.meaning: a group of closely related species
items.example: The superspecies is split into three geographical species.
items.exampleCN: 这个超种被分成三个地理物种。

items.example: Botany ranks variety below subspecies.
items.exampleCN: 植物学把变种排在亚种之下。

definition_en: an organized set of categories and rules used to sort things into groups according to shared features
core_image: 一排排抽屉把混杂的标本按标签分成层级，每个抽屉里还有更小的格子
scene: 图书馆把全部藏书放进一套按学科逐级细分的分类系统，读者据此从大门一直走到具体书架。 The library placed its whole collection in a classification system that divides subjects level by level, so a reader can walk from the entrance to a single shelf.
sceneCN: 这里 classification system 是「分类系统」（第 1 个义项：按共同特征把事物分组的整套体系）；句意：图书馆把全部藏书放进一套按学科逐级细分的分类系统，读者据此可以从大门走到具体书架。

pos.zh: 分类系统；分类体系（可数，复数 classification systems）

senses.title: A general system for sorting by shared features
senses.titleCN: 按共同特征分组的通用体系
senses.definition: an organized scheme of categories, rules and criteria that places similar things together and separates unlike ones
senses.definitionCN: 由类别、规则与判据组成的有序方案，把相似之物放在一起、把不同之物分开
senses.example: Every herbarium depends on a classification system that anyone can learn.
senses.exampleCN: 每一座标本馆都依赖一套人人可学的分类系统。
senses.why: The phrase names a scheme rather than a single act: classification is the sorting, system is the ordered whole, and together they mean a sorting that can be repeated by others.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语指一套方案而非一次动作：classification 是归类，system 是有序整体，合起来就是别人也能重复使用的归类办法。

senses.title: The biological classification system
senses.definition: the hierarchical scheme of kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus and species used for living things
senses.definitionCN: 用于生物界的层级方案：界、门、纲、目、科、属、种
senses.example: Linnaeus gave biology a classification system still visible in every field guide.
senses.exampleCN: 林奈为生物学提供了一套至今仍见于每本野外图鉴的分类系统。
senses.why: Biology needed a stable address for every organism, and a ranked hierarchy supplies one: each level narrows the group until a single kind remains.
senses.whyCN: 生物学需要为每种生物提供稳定地址，而分级层级正好提供：每一级都收窄范围，直到只剩一个种类。

senses.title: A library classification system
senses.definition: a scheme such as Dewey Decimal or Library of Congress that assigns every subject a notation and a shelf position
senses.definitionCN: 如杜威十进分类法或国会图书馆分类法那样，为每个学科分配标记与架位的方案
senses.example: The library's classification system puts astronomy beside mathematics.
senses.exampleCN: 该馆的分类系统把天文学排在数学旁边。
senses.why: A library is a physical place, so its system must do two jobs at once: group related subjects and produce an address that a reader can walk to.
senses.whyCN: 图书馆是物理空间，因此其系统要同时做两件事：把相关学科聚在一起，并给出读者可以走到的地址。

senses.title: A records or information classification system
senses.titleCN: 档案与信息的分类系统
senses.definition: a controlled scheme for labelling documents, data or records so that they can be stored, found and protected consistently
senses.definitionCN: 为文件、数据或档案设定受控标签的方案，使其能被一致地存放、查找与保护
senses.example: The archive adopted a classification system with four security levels.
senses.exampleCN: 该档案馆采用了一套含四个密级的分类系统。
senses.why: Once records outnumber people, sorting becomes an information problem: the system must be closed enough that two clerks file the same paper in the same place.
senses.whyCN: 当档案数量超过人手，归类就成了信息问题：系统必须足够封闭，使两个职员把同一份文件归到同一处。

senses.title: The periodic table as a classification system
senses.titleCN: 作为分类系统的元素周期表
senses.definition: the arrangement of chemical elements by atomic number and recurring properties, which predicts missing members
senses.definitionCN: 按原子序数与周期性性质排列化学元素的方案，并能预测尚未发现的成员
senses.example: Mendeleev's classification system left gaps that later elements filled.
senses.exampleCN: 门捷列夫的分类系统留下的空格后来被新元素填满。
senses.why: A good classification system is judged by what it predicts: the periodic table did not merely sort elements, it told chemists where to look next.
senses.whyCN: 好的分类系统以其预测能力受评判：周期表不只是给元素排序，还告诉化学家下一步该去哪里找。

senses.title: Social classification and its disputes
senses.definition: a scheme that assigns people to categories such as race, class or caste, together with the political questions it raises
senses.definitionCN: 把人归入种族、阶级或种姓等类别的方案，以及由此引出的政治问题
senses.example: Census categories rest on a classification system that changes with politics.
senses.exampleCN: 人口普查的类别依赖一套随政治而变的分类系统。
senses.why: When the things sorted are people, the system stops being neutral: the categories shape how resources and rights are distributed, so every revision is contested.
senses.whyCN: 当被归类的是人时，系统就不再中性：类别影响资源与权利的分配，因此每次修订都会引发争论。

senses.title: A label taxonomy in machine learning
senses.titleCN: 机器学习中的标签体系
senses.definition: the fixed set of labels and their hierarchy used to train and evaluate an automatic classifier
senses.definitionCN: 用于训练与评估自动分类器的固定标签集合及其层级
senses.example: The model's accuracy depends on a consistent classification system.
senses.exampleCN: 模型的准确率取决于一套前后一致的分类系统。
senses.why: A learner can only predict labels it was given, so the human-made system becomes part of the model: unclear categories produce unclear predictions.
senses.whyCN: 学习器只能预测被给定的标签，因此人造的系统成了模型的一部分：类别不清，预测也清不了。

senses.title: A standard coding scheme in commerce
senses.titleCN: 商业中的标准编码体系
senses.definition: an agreed scheme of product or industry codes that lets firms, customs and statistics refer to the same category
senses.definitionCN: 商定好的产品、行业编码方案，使企业、海关与统计部门指向同一类别
senses.example: Customs forms follow an international classification system for goods.
senses.exampleCN: 海关表格遵循一套国际商品分类系统。
senses.why: Trade needs categories that mean the same thing in two countries, so the system is negotiated and written into law rather than left to local habit.
senses.whyCN: 贸易需要两国都理解为同一意义的类别，因此这套系统经过协商并写入法律，而不能交给地方习惯。

senses.title: A classification system as a working tool
senses.titleCN: 作为工作工具的分类系统
senses.definition: the practical version of a scheme, judged by whether users can apply it quickly and agree on the result
senses.definitionCN: 方案的实际使用形态，以使用者能否快速套用并得到一致结果来评判
senses.example: Fieldworkers simplified the classification system to three easily told apart groups.
senses.exampleCN: 野外工作者把分类系统简化为三个容易分辨的类群。
senses.why: A system that cannot be applied in the field fails even if it is logically neat; usability, not elegance, is the final test.
senses.whyCN: 无法在野外应用的系统即使逻辑整齐也告失败；可用性而非优雅才是最终检验。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin-derived noun and a Greek-derived noun: classification from Latin classis and facere, system from Greek systema. Both parts entered English through French or learned Latin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁来源的名词与希腊来源的名词接在一起：classification 出自拉丁 classis 与 facere，system 出自希腊 systema。两部分都经由法语或学术拉丁进入英语。年代为约数。

items.en: Classis meant a division of the Roman people, later a fleet or a group; the sense 'a group of things' is the base of classify.
items.cn: classis 指罗马人的一个等级划分，后指舰队或一组；「一组事物」这一义是 classify 的基础。

items.en: The verb facere 'to make, do' produced the -ficare ending of classificare, so classify literally means 'to make a class of'.
items.cn: 动词 facere「做、造」构成 classificare 的词尾 -ficare，因此 classify 字面就是「使成为一类」。

items.en: Systema meant 'a whole composed of parts', from syn- 'together' plus histanai 'to stand'; Latin took it as systema.
items.cn: systema 意为「由部分组成的整体」，来自 syn-「共同」加 histanai「立」；拉丁语借作 systema。

items.en: In the seventeenth century system was applied to ordered schemes of knowledge, and classification became its natural partner.
items.cn: 17 世纪，system 开始用于知识的有序方案，classification 于是成为它的天然搭档。

items.en: Linnaeus gave the phrase its biological career, and the ranked hierarchy became the model for other classification systems.
items.cn: 林奈让这个短语在生物学中立足，分级层级也成为其他分类系统的样板。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact date when the two words were first used together as a fixed phrase is not fixed here, and the pre-Latin origins of classis are disputed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这两个词最早作为固定短语连用的确切年代此处无法确定；classis 在拉丁语之前的来源亦有争议。

note.en: Group one separates the words that look like classification system; group two compares the neighbouring schemes and their parts.
note.cn: 第一组区分看似「分类系统」的各个词；第二组比较相邻的方案及其组成部分。

entries.definition: The act or result of sorting, without the ordered whole. A classification system is the scheme that makes the act repeatable.
entries.definitionCN: 归类的动作或结果，不含有序整体。分类系统则是使这一动作可重复的方案。

entries.definition: A person or program that assigns items to classes. It uses a classification system rather than being one.
entries.definitionCN: 把人或程序归入类别的施事者。它使用分类系统，本身不是系统。

entries.definition: Relating to classification, as in classificatory kinship. It describes, while the phrase names a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 与分类有关的，如分类式亲属称谓。它是形容词，而这个短语指一个事物。

entries.definition: One level of a biological or social scheme. It is a single box, not the whole arrangement of boxes.
entries.definitionCN: 生物或社会方案中的一级。它是单独的格子，不是全部格子的安排。

entries.definition: The science or practice of naming and ordering groups, especially living things; the system is its product.
entries.definitionCN: 命名与排列类群的科学或实践，尤指生物；分类系统是它的产物。

entries.definition: The set of rules and names themselves, not the grouping logic. A system can be sound while its names are being revised.
entries.definitionCN: 规则与名称本身，而非分组逻辑。系统可以健全，而名称仍在修订。

entries.definition: Outside biology the word names any scheme of categories, which makes it a near synonym of classification system in general use.
entries.definitionCN: 在生物学之外，这个词泛指任何类别方案，因此在日常用法中近乎 classification system 的同义词。

entries.definition: A scheme built from ideal types rather than from ranked groups; it sorts by pattern rather than by descent.
entries.definitionCN: 由理想类型而非分级群体构成的方案；按模式而非按谱系归类。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: classis 'a division' + facere 'to make' + systema 'an organized whole'.
normal.cn: classis「划分」+ facere「做」+ systema「有序整体」。

normal.en: The biological version is the ranked ladder: kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.
normal.cn: 生物学版本就是那架分级梯子：界、门、纲、目、科、属、种。

normal.en: A library system must give a walkable address, so notation and shelf order belong to it.
normal.cn: 图书馆系统必须给出可以走到的地址，因此标记法与架位顺序属于它的一部分。

normal.en: The periodic table is the classic proof that a good system predicts what is missing.
normal.cn: 周期表是「好系统能预测缺项」的经典证据。

normal.en: In machine learning the system is the label set, and its quality limits the model's quality.
normal.cn: 在机器学习中，系统就是标签集合，其质量限制模型的质量。

abstract.en: Picture a building with numbered floors, corridors and doors, so anyone can be sent to one room.
abstract.cn: 想象一座楼有编号的层、走廊与门，任何人都能被指到某一个房间。

abstract.en: Picture a set of coat hooks: each coat hangs where its label says, and no two labels collide.
abstract.cn: 想象一排衣帽钩：每件外套挂在标签所指处，没有两个标签相撞。

abstract.en: Picture a map whose legend is agreed by everyone who uses it, so two travellers read the same terrain.
abstract.cn: 想象一张图例被所有使用者认可的地图，两位旅人因此读到同样的地形。

examples.en: The new classification system replaced a century of ad hoc shelf marks.
examples.cn: 新的分类系统取代了沿用百年的临时架标。

examples.en: No classification system can be revised without moving some books.
examples.cn: 任何分类系统的修订都不可能不移动一些书。

examples.en: Students learn the classification system before they learn any single species name.
examples.cn: 学生先学分类系统，再学任何一个物种的名称。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「class 分类 + system 系统」——把万物分好类的一整套架子 → classification system 分类系统

root: 拉丁 classis「划分、等级」+ facere「做」（构成 classify）与希腊 systema「由部分组成的整体」；两词合为固定短语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of classification system move from the general scheme to the biological ladder, the library shelf, the archive, the periodic table, social categories, machine labels, trade codes and finally to usability as the test of any scheme.
sensesIntro.cn: classification system 的九个义项从通用方案出发，依次落到生物阶梯、图书馆书架、档案馆、周期表、社会类别、机器标签、贸易编码，最后把可用性当作一切方案的检验。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cabinet of labelled drawers, each drawer opening into smaller labelled boxes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一柜贴好标签的抽屉，每个抽屉打开后还有更小的标签盒。

branches.en: THE GENERAL SCHEME: categories, rules and criteria that make sorting repeatable.
branches.cn: 通用方案：使归类可重复的类别、规则与判据。

branches.en: THE TWO CLASSIC CASES: living things get a ranked ladder, books get a walkable address.
branches.cn: 两个经典情形：生物得到分级梯子，图书得到可以走到的地址。

branches.en: CONTROL AND COMMERCE: archives need closed labels, trade needs categories agreed across borders.
branches.cn: 控制与商业：档案需要封闭标签，贸易需要跨国同意的类别。

branches.en: PREDICTION: the periodic table shows that a good system says where to look next.
branches.cn: 预测：周期表表明好系统会指出下一步该去哪里找。

branches.en: WHEN THE SYSTEM MEETS PEOPLE: social categories are contested, machine labels limit models, and field use decides whether a scheme survives.
branches.cn: 系统遇到人时：社会类别引发争论，机器标签限制模型，野外使用决定方案能否存活。

intro.en: The phrase is a partnership of two learned borrowings, one Latin and one Greek, and each part can be read on its own.
intro.cn: 这个短语是两个学术借词的组合，一个来自拉丁，一个来自希腊，每一部分都可单独读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin classis gives class, classic and classify; facere gives -fication in classification; Greek systema gives system and systematic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 classis 给出 class、classic、classify；facere 给出 classification 中的 -fication；希腊 systema 给出 system 与 systematic。

items.example: Classis named the first division before it named a school room.
items.exampleCN: classis 先指划分，后指教室。

items.example: The -ficare ending turns a class into a verb.
items.exampleCN: -ficare 词尾把「类」变成动词。

items.meaning: the act or result of sorting
items.example: Classification precedes the system it is built into.
items.exampleCN: 归类先于它被编入的系统。

items.example: A system holds the categories together.
items.exampleCN: 系统把各个类别维系在一起。

items.example: Clerks classify each new specimen on arrival.
items.exampleCN: 标本到达时由职员逐一归类。

items.example: Classificatory disputes delay every revision.
items.exampleCN: 分类上的分歧使每次修订都拖延。

items.meaning: one who or that which sorts
items.example: The classifier accepts only the labels it was trained on.
items.exampleCN: 分类器只接受它受训过的标签。

items.example: A systematic survey finds what casual collecting misses.
items.exampleCN: 系统的调查能找到随意采集所漏掉的东西。

items.example: One class is a single box in the scheme.
items.exampleCN: 一个 class 只是方案中的一个格子。

senses.title: The science of naming and arranging organisms
senses.titleCN: 命名与排列生物的科学
senses.definition: the branch of biology concerned with describing organisms, naming them and placing them in groups
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中负责描述生物、为其命名并把它们归入类群的分支
senses.example: Taxonomy begins with a specimen and ends with a name that others can use.
senses.exampleCN: 分类学从一份标本开始，以别人也能使用的名称结束。
senses.why: Greek taxis 'arrangement' plus nomos 'law' names a law-governed arrangement: the science exists because names must be assigned by rule, not by preference.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 taxis「排列」加 nomos「法则」点明这是一种受规则支配的排列：这门学问之所以存在，是因为名称必须按规则而非按偏好分配。

senses.title: Any ordered scheme of categories
senses.definition: an ordered set of categories used outside biology, such as a taxonomy of errors, skills or documents
senses.definitionCN: 生物学之外使用的有序类别集合，如错误、技能或文件的分类体系
senses.example: The team built a taxonomy of failure modes before designing the test.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在设计测试之前先建立了一套失效模式分类体系。
senses.why: The Greek sense is general arrangement, so the word travels easily: wherever categories are ordered by rule, the same noun applies.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语原义就是一般的排列，因此这个词迁移得很容易：只要类别按规则排序，同一个名词就适用。

senses.title: The Linnaean ranked hierarchy
senses.definition: the ranked ladder of kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus and species as practised since the eighteenth century
senses.definitionCN: 自 18 世纪以来实行的分级梯子：界、门、纲、目、科、属、种
senses.example: Linnaean taxonomy gave every organism a place in one nested ladder.
senses.exampleCN: 林奈式分类学给每种生物在一架嵌套梯子上安排了位置。
senses.why: A nested ladder answers two needs at once: it shows which groups are inside which, and it gives each rank a name that can be cited.
senses.whyCN: 嵌套梯子同时满足两个需要：它显示哪些类群包含在哪些类群之内，并给每一级一个可被引用的名称。

senses.title: Alpha taxonomy: describing new species
senses.definition: the first-hand work of collecting specimens, describing them and publishing new names, before broader evolutionary questions are asked
senses.definitionCN: 在提出更大的演化问题之前，采集标本、加以描述并发表新名称的一线工作
senses.example: Alpha taxonomy still adds hundreds of beetle names each year.
senses.exampleCN: 甲级分类学每年仍增加数百个甲虫名称。
senses.why: The field distinguishes the first job from the later synthesis: alpha taxonomy produces the units that all other work depends on.
senses.whyCN: 这一领域把最初的工作与后来的综合区分开：甲级分类学生产出所有其他工作都依赖的单位。

senses.title: Numerical taxonomy and phenetics
senses.titleCN: 数值分类学与表型分类
senses.definition: the attempt to build classifications by measuring many characters and clustering them mathematically, rather than by expert judgement
senses.definitionCN: 通过测量大量性状并用数学方法聚类来建立分类，而非依赖专家判断的尝试
senses.example: Numerical taxonomy treats every character as a measured value.
senses.exampleCN: 数值分类学把每个性状当作一个测量值。
senses.why: Twentieth-century computing made it possible to replace the expert's eye with a matrix of measurements, and the phrase marks that shift.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的计算机使人们可以用测量矩阵取代专家的眼光，这一短语正是那次转变的标记。

senses.title: Molecular and phylogenetic taxonomy
senses.titleCN: 分子与系统发生分类学
senses.definition: classification built from DNA sequences and reconstructed evolutionary relationships rather than from outward form alone
senses.definitionCN: 依据脱氧核糖核酸序列与重建的演化关系、而非仅凭外部形态建立的分类
senses.example: Molecular taxonomy overturned groupings that had rested on shape alone.
senses.exampleCN: 分子分类学推翻了仅凭外形建立的类群。
senses.why: Once sequence data became cheap, kinship could be read directly, so the science shifted from comparing forms to comparing inherited letters.
senses.whyCN: 当序列数据变得廉价，亲缘关系可以直接读出，这门学问便从比较形态转向比较可遗传的字母串。

senses.title: Bloom's taxonomy in education
senses.titleCN: 教育学中的布鲁姆分类体系
senses.definition: the ordered list of cognitive skills from remembering to creating, used to write learning objectives and test questions
senses.definitionCN: 从记忆到创造的认知技能有序清单，用于撰写学习目标与试题
senses.example: The syllabus was rewritten around Bloom's taxonomy.
senses.exampleCN: 教学大纲围绕布鲁姆分类体系重写。
senses.why: Here the arranged things are mental skills rather than organisms, but the logic is identical: simple operations sit below complex ones.
senses.whyCN: 这里被排列的是心智技能而非生物，但逻辑完全相同：简单操作位于复杂操作之下。

senses.title: A taxonomy in information architecture
senses.titleCN: 信息架构中的分类体系
senses.definition: the scheme by which a website, archive or database organizes its contents so that users can find them
senses.definitionCN: 网站、档案馆或数据库组织内容、使用户能够找到的分类方案
senses.example: The site's taxonomy split support pages by product rather than by problem.
senses.exampleCN: 该网站的分类体系按产品而非按问题划分支持页面。
senses.why: Digital collections borrowed the word because they face the same task as a museum: many objects, one findable order.
senses.whyCN: 数字收藏借用这个词，因为它们面对与博物馆相同的任务：物件很多，却要有一套可找到的次序。

senses.title: The politics of taxonomy
senses.definition: the social and ethical dimension of deciding which groups are recognized, merged or left unnamed
senses.definitionCN: 决定哪些类群被承认、被合并或不被命名的社会与伦理维度
senses.example: The taxonomy of the group was revised along with the political vocabulary.
senses.exampleCN: 该群体的分类体系随着政治词汇一同被修订。
senses.why: Because a name makes a group visible, the act of classifying is never purely technical; recognition and resources follow the categories.
senses.whyCN: 由于名称使一个类群可见，分类这一行为从来不只是技术性的；承认与资源都会随类别而来。

intro.en: Taxonomy is a Greek compound coined in the nineteenth century: taxis 'arrangement, order' plus nomos 'law, custom'. It has no inherited Latin ancestor, so latinEntries holds only New Latin coinages built from the Greek pieces.
intro.cn: taxonomy 是 19 世纪依希腊语造的复合词：taxis「排列、次序」加 nomos「法则、惯例」。它没有承继而来的拉丁语祖先，因此拉丁词条列表只收由这些希腊成分造成的新拉丁语词。

items.en: Taxis meant 'arrangement, order, battle line', from tassein 'to arrange'. The military sense shows that the word began with ordered placement.
items.cn: taxis 意为「排列、次序、战阵」，出自 tassein「排列」。军事义表明这个词最初就与有序安置有关。

items.en: Nomos meant 'law, custom, usage'. It supplied the second half of many learned compounds, from astronomy to economy.
items.cn: nomos 意为「法则、惯例、用法」，是许多学术复合词的后半部分，从 astronomy 到 economy 皆是。

items.en: Augustin Pyramus de Candolle coined taxonomie in French in 1813 for the theory of plant classification; English took the word soon after.
items.cn: 德堪多在 1813 年以法语 taxonomie 指植物分类的理论；英语随后借入。

items.en: The word expanded from plants to all organisms and then to any ordered scheme of categories.
items.cn: 这个词从植物扩展到全部生物，再扩展到任何有序的类别体系。

items.en: Numerical and molecular methods rebuilt the practice in the twentieth century, but the name of the science did not change.
items.cn: 数值方法与分子方法在 20 世纪重建了这门学问的做法，但学科名称并未改变。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first English printing is not fixed here, and the pre-Greek origin of tassein is a reconstruction rather than an attested form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：taxonomy 最早的英语印刷记录此处无法确定；tassein 在希腊语之前的来源属重构形式，而非有据可查的形式。

note.en: Group one separates words built on the Greek taxis stock; group two compares the neighbouring disciplines and their products.
note.cn: 第一组区分同出希腊 taxis 词干的词；第二组比较相邻学科及其产物。

entries.definition: A single named group at any rank, the object taxonomy works on. The science is the activity, a taxon is its unit.
entries.definitionCN: 任一阶元上被命名的单个类群，是分类学处理的对象。学科是活动，taxon 是其单位。

entries.definition: The mounting of animal skins, from taxis 'arrangement' plus derma 'skin'. It shares the first element but has nothing to do with naming by law.
entries.definitionCN: 制作动物皮张标本，来自 taxis「排列」加 derma「皮」。它共用第一个成分，但与依法命名无关。

entries.definition: An older variant of taxonomic, still found in nineteenth-century titles. It is the same adjective, not another term.
entries.definitionCN: taxonomic 的较老异体，仍见于 19 世纪标题。它是同一个形容词，不是另一个术语。

entries.definition: Relating to taxonomy. The noun names the science, the adjective describes anything belonging to it.
entries.definitionCN: 与分类学有关的。名词指学科，形容词描述属于该学科的事物。

entries.definition: The body of rules and the names produced under them. Taxonomy includes nomenclature but also the grouping decisions.
entries.definitionCN: 规则总体及依规则产生的名称。分类学包含命名法，但也包含分组判断。

entries.definition: The act of placing things into classes. Taxonomy is the science that justifies and stabilizes such acts.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物归入类别的动作。分类学是使这类动作有据可依并稳定下来的学问。

entries.definition: Classification informed by evolutionary history, often used for the broader field in modern biology.
entries.definitionCN: 依据演化历史的分类，现代生物学中常用来指更宽的领域。

entries.definition: A scheme of ideal types rather than ranks fixed by a code; it sorts by pattern and is often qualitative.
entries.definitionCN: 以理想类型而非法规固定阶元构成的方案；按模式归类，常为定性研究。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: taxis 'arrangement' + nomos 'law': taxonomy is arrangement under rules.
normal.cn: taxis「排列」+ nomos「法则」：taxonomy 就是受规则约束的排列。

normal.en: The basic unit is the taxon, and every taxon needs a name that follows a code.
normal.cn: 基本单位是 taxon，每个分类单元都需要一个符合法规的名称。

normal.en: Alpha taxonomy describes; systematics reconstructs; nomenclature names. Three jobs, one neighbourhood.
normal.cn: 甲级分类学负责描述，系统学负责重建，命名法负责命名。三项工作，同一个邻域。

normal.en: Bloom's taxonomy shows the word's reach: mental skills can be ranked just as organisms can.
normal.cn: 布鲁姆分类体系显示了这个词的覆盖面：心智技能也能像生物一样被分级。

normal.en: Molecular taxonomy reads kinship from sequences instead of from shape.
normal.cn: 分子分类学从序列而非外形读出亲缘关系。

abstract.en: Picture a library where every book is shelved by a rule that a stranger can also follow.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，每本书都按一条陌生人也能遵循的规则上架。

abstract.en: Picture a family tree drawn in the air above a cabinet of specimens.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵家谱树悬在标本柜上方。

abstract.en: Picture a court where names are granted by law rather than claimed by whoever speaks first.
abstract.cn: 想象一个法庭，名称依法授予，而不是由先开口的人自行主张。

examples.en: Taxonomy cannot settle every case, because the rank at which two forms differ is a decision.
examples.cn: 分类学无法解决每一个个案，因为两个类型在哪个阶元上算不同，是一个决定。

examples.en: The revised taxonomy moved the genus into a different family.
examples.cn: 修订后的分类体系把这个属移到了另一个科。

examples.en: Field guides are taxonomy made portable for people who are not taxonomists.
examples.cn: 野外图鉴是把分类学做成便携形式，供非分类学者使用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「taxi 出租车 + nomy 规则」——按规则把车排好队 → taxonomy 分类学

root: 希腊语 taxis「排列、次序」+ nomos「法则、惯例」，19 世纪依此造成；无承继的拉丁语祖先，拉丁词条列表只收新拉丁语造词。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of taxonomy run from the biological science through any ordered scheme, the Linnaean ladder, the first-hand description of species, numerical and molecular methods, Bloom's skills, digital architecture and finally the politics of naming.
sensesIntro.cn: taxonomy 的九个义项从生物科学出发，经过任何有序体系、林奈阶梯、一线新种描述、数值与分子方法、布鲁姆技能清单、数字信息架构，最后落到命名的政治面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ladder of names, each rung narrower than the one above, all fixed by rule.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架名称的梯子，每一级都比上一级更窄，且都由规则固定。

branches.en: THE SCIENCE AND ITS LADDER: naming and ranking organisms inside one nested hierarchy.
branches.cn: 学科与其梯子：在一个嵌套层级内为生物命名并分级。

branches.en: THE GENERAL SCHEME: ordered categories travel outside biology into documents and websites.
branches.cn: 通用方案：有序类别走出生物学，进入文件与网站。

branches.en: THE WORK: alpha taxonomy describes new units, numerical taxonomy measures them.
branches.cn: 工作：甲级分类学描述新单位，数值分类学测量它们。

branches.en: THE DEEP EVIDENCE: molecular data replaced shape with sequence as the source of kinship.
branches.cn: 深层证据：分子数据以序列取代外形，成为亲缘关系的来源。

branches.en: THE WIDER LIFE: skills can be ranked, and names carry recognition and power.
branches.cn: 更广的生命：技能也能分级，而名称带来承认与权力。

intro.en: Taxonomy is Greek in both halves and modern in its assembly; the pieces are ancient, the compound is nineteenth-century.
intro.cn: taxonomy 前后两半都来自希腊语，组合却是近代的：成分古老，复合词属 19 世纪。

latinIntro.en: There is no inherited Latin noun for this science; the only Latin entries are New Latin coinages, taxon and taxonomia, built from Greek pieces.
latinIntro.cn: 这门学问没有承继而来的拉丁名词；拉丁词条列表所收仅为由希腊成分造成的新拉丁语词 taxon 与 taxonomia。

items.example: Taxis supplies the ordering half of the word.
items.exampleCN: taxis 提供这个词中「排列」的一半。

items.example: Nomos supplies the rule that makes ordering lawful.
items.exampleCN: nomos 提供使排列有法可依的规则。

items.meaning: a named group at any rank
items.meaningCN: 任一阶元上被命名的类群
items.example: Each taxon must have a valid name.
items.exampleCN: 每个分类单元都必须有有效名称。

items.example: Taxonomy places the specimen in a named rank.
items.exampleCN: 分类学把标本放进一个有名称的阶元。

items.example: The taxonomic decision was published last year.
items.exampleCN: 这项分类学决定去年已发表。

items.example: The taxonomist described forty new species.
items.exampleCN: 这位分类学家描述了四十个新种。

items.example: Taxidermy shares taxis but not nomos.
items.exampleCN: taxidermy 共用 taxis，却不含 nomos。

items.example: Systematics supplies the tree that taxonomy names.
items.exampleCN: 系统学提供分类学所要命名的树。

items.meaning: the system of names and rules
items.example: Nomenclature governs the form of every name.
items.exampleCN: 命名法管着每个名称的形式。

latinEntries.structure: taxon, taxonis (n., New Latin, from Greek taxis)

definition_en: relating to taxonomy or to the classification of organisms into ranks
core_image: 同一排标本盒的盖子上写着分属不同层级的名称牌，牌子之间有细线相连
scene: 两位研究者争论这批甲虫应归入哪一个分类阶元，最后决定维持原来的位置。 The two researchers argued over the taxonomic rank of the beetles and finally kept their original placement.
sceneCN: 这里 taxonomic 是「分类上的」（第 2 个义项：与分类阶元有关的）；句意：两位研究者争论这批甲虫应归入哪一个分类阶元，最后决定维持原来的位置。

derivatives.zh: 从分类学角度；按分类学方法
分类学的（较少用的异体）
副分类学的（由受过训练的技术人员做的分类工作）

senses.title: Relating to taxonomy as a science
senses.titleCN: 与分类学这门学问有关
senses.definition: belonging to or derived from the science that names and arranges organisms
senses.definitionCN: 属于或出自命名与排列生物这门学问的
