senses.example: The paper opens with a taxonomic question, not an ecological one.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文以分类学问题而非生态学问题开篇。
senses.why: Taxonomy plus the Greek adjective ending -ic produces a word that simply means 'of that science'; the ending adds no new meaning of its own.
senses.whyCN: taxonomy 加希腊形容词词尾 -ic 构成一个只表示「属于那门学问」的词；词尾本身不增添新义。

senses.title: Relating to a rank or level
senses.definition: connected with a particular level in the hierarchy, such as family, genus or species
senses.definitionCN: 与层级中的某一级有关的，如科、属或种
senses.example: The dispute was about taxonomic rank rather than about biology.
senses.exampleCN: 争论针对的是分类阶元，而不是生物学本身。
senses.why: Ranks are the skeleton of the system, so 'taxonomic rank' is the standard phrase for the level at which a group is placed.
senses.whyCN: 阶元是这套体系的骨架，因此 taxonomic rank 是把类群安置在某一级时的标准说法。

senses.title: Relating to a scientific name
senses.definition: connected with the formal name of a group and the rules that govern it
senses.definitionCN: 与类群的正式名称及管束该名称的规则有关的
senses.example: A taxonomic name is italicized and tied to a type specimen.
senses.exampleCN: 分类学名称用斜体，并与模式标本绑定。
senses.why: A name is not a label chosen for convenience; it is a ruling with a type behind it, which is why the adjective is used for the name itself.
senses.whyCN: 名称不是为方便而选的标签，而是背后有模式标本支撑的裁定，因此这里用这个形容词来限定名称。

senses.title: Relating to a distinguishing character
senses.definition: connected with a feature that is used to separate one group from another
senses.definitionCN: 与用来把某个类群与另一个类群区分开的特征有关的
senses.example: Wing venation is the main taxonomic character in this family.
senses.exampleCN: 翅脉是这个科的主要分类性状。
senses.why: A character becomes taxonomic only when it is shown to mark a group rather than an individual, so the adjective marks a role, not a kind of feature.
senses.whyCN: 一个性状只有在被证明标记的是类群而非个体时才算分类性状，因此这个形容词标的是角色，而不是某类特征。

senses.title: Relating to a group so defined
senses.titleCN: 与如此定义的类群有关
senses.definition: connected with a group that has been formally delimited, as in taxonomic group or taxonomic assemblage
senses.definitionCN: 与已被正式界定的一组生物有关的，如分类群
senses.example: The wetlands hold a rich taxonomic assemblage of diatoms.
senses.exampleCN: 这些湿地拥有种类丰富的硅藻分类群。
senses.why: Once a group is delimited by rule, it can be counted and compared; the adjective signals that the grouping is official rather than casual.
senses.whyCN: 一旦类群按规则被界定，就可以计数与比较；这个形容词表明该分组是正式的，而不是随意的。

senses.title: Relating to a revision of classification
senses.definition: connected with the formal act of re-examining and changing the placement of groups
senses.definitionCN: 与重新审查并改变类群位置的正式行为有关的
senses.example: The taxonomic revision split one genus into three.
senses.exampleCN: 这次分类修订把一个属拆成了三个。
senses.why: Revision is the part of the science where judgement is public: the adjective marks work that reopens settled placements.
senses.whyCN: 修订是这门学问中判断公开化的一环：这个形容词标记的是重新打开既有安置的工作。

senses.title: Relating to diversity measured by taxa
senses.titleCN: 与按类群衡量的多样性有关
senses.definition: connected with diversity counted as the number and spread of higher groups rather than of species alone
senses.definitionCN: 与按较高级类群的数量与分布而非仅按物种数衡量的多样性有关的
senses.example: Taxonomic diversity fell long before species numbers did.
senses.exampleCN: 分类多样性在物种数下降之前很久就已下降。
senses.why: Counting families or phyla answers a different question from counting species, so the adjective distinguishes the scale of the measure.
senses.whyCN: 教科数或门数回答的是与教物种数不同的问题，因此这个形容词区分了度量的尺度。

senses.title: Relating to authority in naming
senses.definition: connected with the person or work whose judgement establishes a name, as in taxonomic authority
senses.definitionCN: 与凭其判断确立一个名称的人或著作有关的，如分类学权威
senses.example: The catalog cites the taxonomic authority after each name.
senses.exampleCN: 目录在每一个名称之后标出分类学权威。
senses.why: In nomenclature a name is tied to the first valid publication, so authority is a technical slot rather than a compliment.
senses.whyCN: 在命名法中，名称与首次有效发表绑定，因此「权威」是一个技术位置，而不是恭维。

senses.title: Used loosely for 'of classification' generally
senses.definition: a looser use in which the word simply means 'having to do with classification', even outside biology
senses.definitionCN: 较宽松的用法，只表示「与分类有关」，即使在生物学之外
senses.example: The report's taxonomic section sorts the failures by cause.
senses.exampleCN: 报告的分类部分按原因给失败情形排序。
senses.why: Because the adjective carries no biological content by itself, it can be borrowed wherever sorting by categories occurs.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个形容词本身不含生物学内容，凡是按类别排序之处都可以借用它。

intro.en: Taxonomic is taxonomy plus the adjective ending -ic, which English received through Latin -icus from Greek -ikos. The word is modern even though both pieces are ancient. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: taxonomic 是 taxonomy 加形容词词尾 -ic；英语经拉丁 -icus 从希腊 -ikos 得到这一词尾。两个成分古老，词本身却是近代的。年代为约数。

items.en: The Greek suffix -ikos formed adjectives of belonging, as in philosophikos 'of a philosopher'; Latin -icus and English -ic continue it.
items.cn: 希腊后缀 -ikos 构成表示归属的形容词，如 philosophikos「哲人的」；拉丁 -icus 与英语 -ic 承接了它。

items.en: The noun taxonomy was coined in 1813 from taxis 'arrangement' and nomos 'law'; the adjective followed the noun.
items.cn: 名词 taxonomy 于 1813 年由 taxis「排列」与 nomos「法则」造成；形容词随后出现。

items.en: Nineteenth-century naturalists needed the adjective for ranks, characters and revisions, and taxonomic spread through the literature.
items.cn: 19 世纪博物学者需要一个形容词来修饰阶元、性状与修订，taxonomic 由此在文献中传开。

items.en: Twentieth-century ecology made taxonomic diversity and taxonomic distinctness standard measures.
items.cn: 20 世纪生态学把分类多样性与分类独特性变成标准度量。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first printing of taxonomic is not fixed here, and the pre-Greek origin of taxis is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：taxonomic 最早的印刷记录此处无法确定；taxis 在希腊语之前的来源属重构。

note.en: Group one separates forms that look like the adjective; group two compares adjectives of neighbouring meaning.
note.cn: 第一组区分外形近似这个形容词的各形；第二组比较意思相邻的形容词。

entries.definition: An older variant of the same adjective, still used by some writers. It means exactly the same and is not a separate term.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词的较老异体，仍有人使用。意思完全相同，并非另一个术语。

entries.definition: The science itself. The adjective describes work or features belonging to it; the noun names the field.
entries.definitionCN: 学问本身。形容词描述属于它的工作或特征；名词指这个领域。

entries.definition: A named group at any rank. Taxonomic work produces and revises taxa, but a taxon is not a description word.
entries.definitionCN: 任一阶元上被命名的类群。分类工作产生并修订分类单元，但 taxon 不是描述性形容词。

entries.definition: Relating to taxidermy, the mounting of skins. It shares taxis 'arrangement' but not nomos 'law'.
entries.definitionCN: 与动物皮张标本制作有关的。它共用 taxis「排列」，但不含 nomos「法则」。

entries.definition: Relating to systematics, which includes evolutionary relationships. Taxonomic work may rest on systematics but does not have to.
entries.definitionCN: 与系统学有关的，包含演化关系。分类工作可以依据系统学，但不必如此。

entries.definition: Relating to the rules and form of names, not to the grouping decision. The two adjectives mark different stages of the work.
entries.definitionCN: 与名称的规则和形式有关，而不涉及分组判断。两个形容词标记工作的不同阶段。

entries.definition: Relating to classification in general, often outside biology. It is broader and less technical than taxonomic.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指与分类有关，常在生物学之外。比 taxonomic 更宽、更不技术化。

entries.definition: Relating to the feature that separates a group in an identification key. It is the practical face of a taxonomic character.
entries.definitionCN: 与检索表中区分类群的特征有关的。它是分类性状在实用层面的对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: taxonomy + -ic: the adjective adds only 'belonging to', so it never carries a new biological claim.
normal.cn: taxonomy + -ic：形容词只增添「属于」之意，因此它从不带来新的生物学主张。

normal.en: The fixed phrases show its range: taxonomic rank, taxonomic name, taxonomic character, taxonomic revision.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示其范围：分类阶元、分类学名称、分类性状、分类修订。

normal.en: Taxonomical is the older variant; both mean the same and neither is wrong.
normal.cn: taxonomical 是较老的异体；两者意思相同，也都不算错。

normal.en: Taxonomic diversity counts higher groups, so it answers a different question from species richness.
normal.cn: 分类多样性数的是较高级类群，因此它回答的问题不同于物种丰富度。

normal.en: Taxidermic shares taxis but not nomos, which is how a look-alike can be a false friend.
normal.cn: taxidermic 共用 taxis 却不含 nomos，形近词因此可能成为假朋友。

abstract.en: Picture a label on a drawer that says not what is inside but which rank the inside belongs to.
abstract.cn: 想象抽屉上的标签不写里面是什么，而写里面属于哪一级。

abstract.en: Picture a referee's whistle: the adjective marks that a decision was made by rule.
abstract.cn: 想象裁判的哨声：这个形容词标记某项决定是按规则作出的。

abstract.en: Picture two nearly identical words standing back to back, sharing a prefix but not a parent.
abstract.cn: 想象两个几乎一样的词背靠背站着，共用前缀却没有共同祖先。

examples.en: The taxonomic position of the group has been disputed for a century.
examples.cn: 这个类群的分类位置已争论了一个世纪。

examples.en: Taxonomic characters must be checked against many specimens before they are trusted.
examples.cn: 分类性状必须对照大量标本检验之后才可采信。

examples.en: She published a taxonomic revision of the entire family.
examples.cn: 她发表了整个科的分类修订。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「taxonomy 分类学 + ic ……的」——分类学上的、分类层面的 → taxonomic 分类学的

root: taxonomy + -ic（希腊 -ikos 经拉丁 -icus 进入英语）；taxonomy 出自希腊 taxis「排列」+ nomos「法则」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of taxonomic all attach the same adjective to different objects: the science, a rank, a name, a character, a group, a revision, a measure of diversity, an authority and finally any sorting at all.
sensesIntro.cn: taxonomic 的九个义项把同一个形容词接到不同对象上：学科、阶元、名称、性状、类群、修订、多样性度量、命名权威，最后是任何分类工作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stamp that reads 'belongs to the classification', pressed onto very different objects.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚写着「属于分类体系」的印章，盖在各种不同的对象上。

branches.en: THE SCIENCE ITSELF: the adjective's plainest job is to mark work as belonging to taxonomy.
branches.cn: 学科本身：这个形容词最基本的用途是把工作标记为属于分类学。

branches.en: THE SKELETON AND THE LABEL: rank and name are the two formal handles of any group.
branches.cn: 骨架与标签：阶元与名称是任何类群的两个正式把手。

branches.en: THE EVIDENCE AND THE RESULT: a character justifies a group, and the group is what gets counted.
branches.cn: 证据与结果：性状为类群提供依据，类群则是被计数的对象。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC ACT: revision reopens placements, authority records who fixed a name.
branches.cn: 公开行为：修订重新打开安置，权威记录谁固定了名称。

branches.en: THE LOOSE USE: diversity at higher ranks, and any sorting outside biology.
branches.cn: 宽松用法：较高级类群的多样性，以及生物学之外的任何分类。

intro.en: Taxonomic is a transparent derivative: a noun of science plus the common adjective ending, with no idiomatic twist.
intro.cn: taxonomic 是透明的派生词：一个学科名词加常见形容词词尾，没有习语性的转折。

latinIntro.en: The Latin contribution is the adjective ending -icus; the noun itself is Greek. New Latin taxon supplies the unit noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的贡献是形容词词尾 -icus；名词本身来自希腊语。新拉丁语 taxon 提供单位名词。

items.example: The adjective is formed directly on the noun.
items.exampleCN: 形容词直接由这个名词构成。

items.example: The ending turns a field into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把领域名变成形容词。

items.example: A taxonomic question comes before an ecological one here.
items.exampleCN: 此处分类学问题先于生态学问题。

items.example: Taxonomical is a variant, not a different concept.
items.exampleCN: taxonomical 是异体，不是不同概念。

items.example: Taxonomically, the two forms are one species.
items.exampleCN: 从分类学上看，这两个类型是一个物种。

items.example: The taxon is the unit the adjective describes.
items.exampleCN: taxon 是这个形容词所描述的单位。

items.example: Taxidermy is a look-alike with a different second element.
items.exampleCN: taxidermy 是第二个成分不同的形近词。

items.example: Systematic work reconstructs the tree; taxonomic work names its branches.
items.exampleCN: 系统学工作重建树，分类学工作为树枝命名。

definition_en: a person who studies, describes and names groups of organisms according to a formal system
core_image: 一位研究者伏在标本柜前，把新到的甲虫一只只摆开，在卡片上写下名称与描述
scene: 在自然史博物馆的标本柜前，一位分类学家把新到的甲虫逐一比对，为它们写出名称与描述。 At the drawers of the natural history museum, a taxonomist compared the newly arrived beetles one by one and wrote names and descriptions for them.
sceneCN: 这里 taxonomist 是「分类学家」（第 1 个义项：从事分类学研究的人）；句意：在自然史博物馆的标本柜前，一位分类学家把新到的甲虫逐一比对，并写出名称与描述。

derivatives.zh: 副分类学家（受训后协助采集与初筛的技术人员）

senses.title: A practitioner of taxonomy
senses.definition: someone who describes organisms, assigns them to ranks and publishes names under the rules of nomenclature
senses.definitionCN: 描述生物、把它们安置到阶元并按命名法规则发表名称的人
senses.example: The taxonomist spent the morning measuring the type series.
senses.exampleCN: 这位分类学家整个上午都在测量模式系列标本。
senses.why: Taxonomy plus -ist names the person by the discipline, in the same pattern as economist or botanist: the suffix means 'one who practises'.
senses.whyCN: taxonomy 加 -ist 以学科命名从业者，与 economist、botanist 同型；词尾意为「从事……的人」。

senses.title: A describer of new species
senses.definition: a person whose work is to recognize an undescribed species and publish its first formal description
senses.definitionCN: 其工作是识别尚未被描述的物种并发表首次正式描述的人
senses.example: A single taxonomist may describe a hundred new species in a career.
senses.exampleCN: 一位分类学家一生可能描述上百个新种。
senses.why: The core act of the job is the first description: without a published name and type, a new species has no place in the system.
senses.whyCN: 这份工作的核心动作是首次描述：没有发表的名称与模式标本，新种在系统中就没有位置。

senses.title: A reviser of existing classifications
senses.definition: a person who re-examines an established group, compares all known material and publishes a changed arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 重新审查一个已建立的类群、比对全部已知材料并发表改变后安排的人
senses.example: The taxonomist revised the family after examining every type in Europe.
senses.exampleCN: 这位分类学家在查看欧洲全部模式标本之后修订了该科。
senses.why: Revision is the second half of the craft: names once published can still be misplaced, and only a full comparison can change them.
senses.whyCN: 修订是这门手艺的后半程：已发表的名称仍可能被放错位置，只有全面比对才能改变它。

senses.title: A curator of collections
senses.definition: a person who cares for museum or herbarium collections and identifies the material that arrives
senses.definitionCN: 管理博物馆或标本馆收藏、并鉴定新到材料的人
senses.example: The taxonomist on duty identified the box of unsorted ferns.
senses.exampleCN: 值班的分类学家鉴定了那箱未分拣的蕨类。
senses.why: Collections are the memory of the science, so many taxonomists work inside museums, where naming and preservation are the same daily task.
senses.whyCN: 收藏是这门学问的记忆，因此许多分类学家在博物馆里工作，命名与保存在那里是同一件日常事务。

senses.title: A field collector and observer
senses.definition: a person who collects specimens and records their habitat, behaviour and variation before naming them
senses.definitionCN: 在命名之前采集标本并记录其生境、行为与变异的人
senses.example: The taxonomist collected along the ridge for three seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 这位分类学家沿山脊采集了三个季节。
senses.why: A name rests on specimens, and good specimens rest on field notes: without locality and habit, the material cannot be interpreted later.
senses.whyCN: 名称依赖标本，好的标本依赖野外记录：没有产地与习性，材料日后无法解读。

senses.title: A molecular taxonomist
senses.definition: a person who uses DNA sequences and phylogenetic methods to test and rebuild groupings
senses.definitionCN: 用脱氧核糖核酸序列与系统发生方法检验并重建类群的人
senses.example: The molecular taxonomist found that the two genera were one.
senses.exampleCN: 这位分子分类学家发现这两个属其实是一个。
senses.why: The job's tools changed but its question did not: what belongs with what. Sequences simply answer it with more letters than measurements.
senses.whyCN: 工具变了，问题没变：什么与什么同属一类。序列只是用更多字母来回答这个问题。

senses.title: The author of a name in citation
senses.definition: the person recorded after a scientific name as its author, a technical slot rather than a rank
senses.definitionCN: 在学名之后被记录为命名者的人，这是技术位置而非职级
senses.example: The label ends with the taxonomist's name and the year.
senses.exampleCN: 标签末尾写着命名者的姓名与年份。
senses.why: Nomenclature ties a name to its first valid publication, so the author's name becomes part of the name's identity and can be cited in court-like precision.
senses.whyCN: 命名法把名称与首次有效发表绑定，因此作者姓名成为名称身份的一部分，可以像法庭记录一样精确引用。

senses.title: An amateur or citizen taxonomist
senses.definition: a volunteer or hobbyist who contributes records and specimens, often specializing in one group
senses.definitionCN: 贡献记录与标本的志愿者或爱好者，常专注于某一个类群
senses.example: Amateur taxonomists supplied half the records used in the atlas.
senses.exampleCN: 业余分类学家提供了图集中一半的记录。
senses.why: The word does not require a salary: expertise is measured by published identifications and reliable records, so hobbyists can stand inside the same noun.
senses.whyCN: 这个词并不要求有薪水：专业程度由已发表的鉴定与可靠记录衡量，因此爱好者也能站在同一个名词之内。

senses.title: A parataxonomist in practice
senses.definition: a technician trained to sort and pre-identify material, extending the reach of a small number of specialists
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、能分拣与初步鉴定材料的技术人员，扩大了少数专家的覆盖面
senses.example: Parataxonomists made the insect survey possible in one season.
senses.exampleCN: 副分类学家使这项昆虫调查在一个季节内完成。
senses.why: When specialists are scarce, the work is split: the prefix para- marks a trained helper who performs part of the task without claiming the full role.
senses.whyCN: 当专家稀缺时，工作会被拆分：前缀 para- 标出一位受过训练的助手，承担部分任务而不自称完整角色。

intro.en: Taxonomist is a nineteenth-century person noun: taxonomy plus -ist. Both pieces are Greek-derived, and the word names a practitioner rather than a theory. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: taxonomist 是 19 世纪的人称名词：taxonomy 加 -ist。两个成分都源自希腊语，这个词命名的是从业者而非理论。年代为约数。

items.en: The base noun joins taxis 'arrangement' to nomos 'law'; the person noun inherits that meaning unchanged.
items.cn: 基础名词把 taxis「排列」与 nomos「法则」结合；人称名词原样继承这一含义。

items.en: The agent suffix -istēs meant 'one who does or follows', and English -ist continues it in economist, botanist and taxonomist.
items.cn: 施事后缀 -istēs 意为「从事或追随……的人」，英语 -ist 在 economist、botanist、taxonomist 中延续了它。

items.en: As natural history split into specialties, the person noun appeared to distinguish the classifier from the collector and the anatomist.
items.cn: 随着博物学分成专门领域，这个人物名词出现，用来把分类者与采集者、解剖者区分开。

items.en: Molecular methods added a new kind of practitioner, but the older noun absorbed it rather than splitting.
items.cn: 分子方法增加了新一类从业者，但旧名词把他吸收进来，而没有分裂出新词。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first printing of taxonomist is not fixed here, and the pre-Greek origin of taxis is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：taxonomist 最早的印刷记录此处无法确定；taxis 在希腊语之前的来源属重构。

note.en: Group one separates the person noun from its relatives; group two compares neighbouring specialist roles.
note.cn: 第一组区分这个人物名词与其同族词；第二组比较相邻的专家角色。

entries.definition: The science, not the person. A taxonomist practises taxonomy, just as an economist practises economics.
entries.definitionCN: 学科，而非人。分类学家从事分类学，正如经济学家从事经济学。

entries.definition: A named group. It is what the person works on, not what the person is.
entries.definitionCN: 被命名的类群。它是此人处理的对象，不是此人的身份。

entries.definition: A person who mounts animal skins, from taxis 'arrangement' and derma 'skin'. The suffix is the same, the root is not.
entries.definitionCN: 制作动物皮张标本的人，来自 taxis「排列」与 derma「皮」。词尾相同，词根不同。

entries.definition: Relating to the science. The adjective describes the work; the person noun names who does it.
entries.definitionCN: 与这门学问有关的。形容词描述工作，人称名词指谁来做。

entries.definition: A specialist in systematics, often concerned with evolutionary relationships as well as names.
entries.definitionCN: 系统学专家，常同时关心演化关系与名称。

entries.definition: A person responsible for a collection; curation overlaps with taxonomy but also covers preservation, loans and display.
entries.definitionCN: 负责收藏的人；管理与分类学重叠，但也包含保存、借展与陈列。

entries.definition: A technician trained to sort and pre-identify specimens, performing part of the taxonomist's task.
entries.definitionCN: 受训后分拣与初步鉴定标本的技术人员，承担分类学家部分工作。

entries.definition: A person who matches a specimen to an existing name. Identification is one act inside the larger job.
entries.definitionCN: 把标本与既有名称对应起来的人。鉴定是较大工作中的一项动作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: taxonomy + -ist, the same pattern as economy/economist and botany/botanist.
normal.cn: taxonomy + -ist，与 economy/economist、botany/botanist 同型。

normal.en: The author's name after a scientific name is the taxonomist's signature in the record.
normal.cn: 学名之后的作者姓名，就是分类学家留在记录上的签名。

normal.en: A type specimen is the voucher that makes a taxonomist's name checkable.
normal.cn: 模式标本是使分类学家的名称可被核查的凭证。

normal.en: Revision, not description alone, occupies much of the working life.
normal.cn: 修订而非仅仅描述，占据了职业生涯的大部分。

normal.en: Parataxonomist splits the role: para- marks a trained helper rather than a lesser species of expert.
normal.cn: parataxonomist 把角色拆开：para- 标出受训助手，而非次一等的专家。

abstract.en: Picture a person holding one beetle against a drawer of a thousand, deciding where it belongs.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把一只甲虫对着装有一千只的抽屉，判断它该归何处。

abstract.en: Picture a signature in the margin of an old page, still the final word on a name.
abstract.cn: 想象旧页边上的一个签名，至今仍是某个名称的最终依据。

abstract.en: Picture a chain of helpers passing specimens up to one desk where the name is written.
abstract.cn: 想象一串助手把标本层层递到一张桌前，名称就在那里写下。

examples.en: The taxonomist's description ran to forty pages and included every measured character.
examples.cn: 这位分类学家的描述长达四十页，包含每一个测量过的性状。

examples.en: No taxonomist had examined the group since the original monograph.
examples.cn: 自最初那本专著之后，再没有分类学家审查过这个类群。

examples.en: The survey depended on two parataxonomists and one taxonomist.
examples.cn: 这次调查依靠两名副分类学家和一名分类学家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「taxonomy 分类学 + ist 人」——做分类学的人 → taxonomist 分类学家

root: taxonomy + -ist（希腊 -istēs）；taxonomy 出自希腊 taxis「排列」+ nomos「法则」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of taxonomist all name the same person under different parts of the role: practitioner, describer, reviser, curator, field collector, molecular worker, cited author, amateur and trained helper.
sensesIntro.cn: taxonomist 的九个义项都指同一个人，只是从角色的不同侧面命名：从业者、描述者、修订者、管理者、野外采集者、分子工作者、被引作者、爱好者与受训助手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at a drawer of specimens, writing a name that others will have to use.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在标本抽屉前，写下一个别人日后必须使用的名称。

branches.en: THE CORE ACT: measure, compare and publish the first description.
branches.cn: 核心动作：测量、比较并发表首次描述。

branches.en: THE KEEPERS: revision and curation keep the system from drifting.
branches.cn: 守护者：修订与管理使系统不致漂移。

branches.en: THE SOURCE: field notes and specimens supply what the name will rest on.
branches.cn: 源头：野外记录与标本提供名称将要依赖的东西。

branches.en: THE NEW TOOLS: sequences test groupings that shape alone could not settle.
branches.cn: 新工具：序列检验仅凭外形无法定论的类群。

branches.en: THE RECORD AND THE WORKFORCE: the author's name becomes part of the name, and amateurs and parataxonomists extend the reach.
branches.cn: 记录与人力：作者姓名成为名称的一部分，爱好者与副分类学家扩大了覆盖面。

intro.en: Taxonomist follows the ordinary agent pattern of English: a discipline noun plus -ist for the person who practises it.
intro.cn: taxonomist 遵循英语常见的施事构词模式：学科名词加 -ist，指从事该学科的人。

latinIntro.en: Latin contributes the agent suffix through -ista, itself from Greek; the base noun is Greek. New Latin taxon supplies the object noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语经 -ista 提供施事后缀（其本身来自希腊语）；基础名词是希腊语。新拉丁语 taxon 提供对象名词。

items.example: The person noun is built directly on the discipline.
items.exampleCN: 人称名词直接建立在学科名上。

items.example: The suffix names a practitioner, as in botanist.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾命名从业者，如 botanist。

items.example: The taxonomist described the new species.
items.exampleCN: 这位分类学家描述了新种。

items.example: Parataxonomists sorted the catch before the specialist arrived.
items.exampleCN: 专家到来之前，副分类学家先分拣了采集物。

items.example: A taxidermist shares the suffix and the first root, not the second.
items.exampleCN: 皮张标本制作者共用词尾与第一个词根，但不共用第二个。

items.example: The systematist drew the tree the taxonomist named.
items.exampleCN: 系统学家画出树，分类学家为其命名。

items.meaning: one who cares for a collection
items.example: The curator and the taxonomist often share one desk.
items.exampleCN: 藏品管理者与分类学家常共用一张桌子。

items.meaning: one who matches specimens to names
items.example: The identifier works from a key, not from a monograph.
items.exampleCN: 鉴定者依据检索表工作，而非依据专著。

definition_zh: 属；（生物分类的）属；逻辑上的属；一类
definition_en: a rank in biological classification above species and below family, or a class that contains subordinate kinds
core_image: 同一排标本盒里装着几种相似的动物，盒盖写着它们共用的名称
scene: 同一属里的几种猫科动物被排在同一排标本盒中，盒盖上写着它们共用的名称。 Several cat species of the same genus are arranged in one row of specimen boxes, with their shared name written on the lids.
sceneCN: 这里 genus 是「属」（第 1 个义项：位于种之上、科之下的分类阶元）；句意：同一属里的几种猫科动物被排在同一排标本盒中，盒盖上写着它们共用的名称。

pos.zh: 属（复数 genera）；逻辑上的属；一类

senses.title: The rank above species
senses.definition: the taxonomic rank that groups one or more species sharing a common ancestor and a set of structural features
senses.definitionCN: 把共享祖先与一组结构特征的一个或多个物种聚合起来的分类阶元
senses.example: The genus contains four species, two of them recently described.
senses.exampleCN: 这个属包含四个物种，其中两个是最近描述的。
senses.why: Latin genus meant 'birth, race, kind'; taxonomy kept 'kind' and gave it a fixed position: a kind that holds smaller kinds.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 genus 意为「出生、族类、种类」；分类学保留了「种类」义，并给它固定位置：一个装更小种类的种类。

senses.title: The first word of a binomial
senses.definition: the capitalized element placed first in the two-part scientific name of a species
senses.definitionCN: 物种两段式学名中置于最前、首字母大写的成分
senses.example: The genus name is capitalized and may be abbreviated after first use.
senses.exampleCN: 属名首字母大写，首次出现之后可以缩写。
senses.why: A binomial is an address written in two words, and the genus is the street while the species epithet is the house.
senses.whyCN: 双名法是用两个词写成的地址：属名是街道，种加词是门牌。

senses.title: The logical genus containing species
senses.definition: in logic, a wider class that contains narrower classes as its species, the relation of genus and species
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑学中作为种的上位、包含较窄类别的较宽类别，即属与种的关系
senses.example: Animal is the genus and bird the species in the old scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧方案中，动物是属，鸟是种。
senses.why: Logic had the pair before biology: genus and species named containment, and Linnaeus borrowed a ready-made ladder.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学早于生物学拥有这对词：属与种表示包含关系，林奈借用的是一架现成的梯子。

senses.title: A kind or class in general
senses.definition: a broad kind of thing, often in the phrase a genus of, where the reference is not biological
senses.definitionCN: 宽泛的一类事物，常用于 a genus of 结构，所指并非生物
senses.example: A genus of problems resisted every standard method.
senses.exampleCN: 有一类问题抵抗所有标准方法。
senses.why: The everyday sense keeps the Latin breadth: any class that holds smaller classes can be called a genus, with or without specimens.
senses.whyCN: 日常义保留了拉丁语的宽度：任何容纳更小类别的类别都可以叫 genus，与标本无关。

senses.title: The plural genera
senses.definition: the Latin third-declension plural, used in English for several genera and often a marker of technical writing
senses.definitionCN: 拉丁第三变格法复数，英语中用来指多个属，也常成为技术写作的标志
senses.example: Three genera were moved into the new family.
senses.exampleCN: 三个属被移入新科。
senses.why: English keeps genera because the Latin plural is fixed in the codes; using genuses marks a speaker as an outsider.
senses.whyCN: 英语保留 genera，因为法规固定了拉丁复数；说 genuses 会显出外行。

senses.title: The type genus of a family
senses.definition: the genus that gives a family its name and fixes the application of that family name
senses.definitionCN: 为某科提供名称、并固定该科名适用范围的那个属
senses.example: The family takes its name from the type genus.
senses.exampleCN: 这个科的名字取自其模式属。
senses.why: Names must be anchored somewhere, and the type genus is that anchor: the family name is built from it and cannot drift away.
senses.whyCN: 名称必须有锚点，模式属就是那个锚：科名由它构成，因此不能漂移。

senses.title: A monotypic genus
senses.definition: a genus that contains only one species, so the genus and the species carry almost the same content
senses.definitionCN: 只含一个物种的属，属与种的内容因此几乎相同
senses.example: The monotypic genus has no second species to compare with.
senses.exampleCN: 这个单型属没有第二个物种可供比较。
senses.why: When a genus holds one species, the rank above adds no information; taxonomists argue whether such genera should be kept.
senses.whyCN: 当一个属只含一个物种时，上一级并不增加信息；分类学家因此争论这样的属是否应当保留。

senses.title: The adjective generic and its drift
senses.titleCN: 派生形容词 generic 的语义漂移
senses.definition: the derived adjective meaning 'of a genus', which has also come to mean 'common to a whole class' and hence 'unbranded'
senses.definitionCN: 派生形容词，意为「属的」，又引申为「整类共有的」，进而指「无品牌的」
senses.example: Generic names on the shelf told the shopper nothing about the maker.
senses.exampleCN: 货架上的通用名称没有告诉顾客任何关于厂家的事。
senses.why: From 'of a kind' to 'shared by the whole kind' to 'having no distinctive mark': the drift is visible in the word generic, not in genus itself.
senses.whyCN: 从「某一类的」到「整类共有的」再到「没有独特标记的」：这一漂移体现在 generic 一词中，而非 genus 本身。

intro.en: Genus is a Latin noun taken into English with its Latin plural genera. It meant 'birth, origin, race, kind' and became the rank above species. Dates are approximate, and the Indo-European root is reconstructed.
intro.cn: genus 是连同拉丁复数 genera 一起进入英语的拉丁名词，意为「出生、起源、族类、种类」，后来成为物种之上的阶元。年代为约数，印欧词根属重构。

items.en: Genus, generis meant 'birth, descent, race, kind'. It was a third-declension neuter noun and already covered both ancestry and category.
items.cn: genus, generis 意为「出生、血统、族类、种类」，是第三变格法中性名词，本已兼指血统与类别。

items.en: The noun is tied to gignere 'to beget, bring forth', which also gives genius, generate and genital.
items.cn: 该名词与 gignere「生育、产生」相关，后者还给出 genius、generate 与 genital。

items.en: The deeper root is reconstructed as *ǵenh₁- 'to beget', also behind Greek genos and Latin gens; the reconstruction is conventional rather than attested.
items.cn: 更深词根被重构为 *ǵenh₁-「生育」，也见于希腊语 genos 与拉丁 gens；这一重构是通行做法，并非有据可查。

items.en: Before biology, genus named the wider class in the pair genus and species, a relation of containment.
items.cn: 在生物学之前，genus 指属种对中的上位类别，是一种包含关系。

items.en: Linnaeus placed genus immediately above species in the eighteenth century and made its name the first word of the binomial.
items.cn: 林奈在 18 世纪把属置于种之上，并让属名成为双名法的第一个词。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the exact English first use is not fixed here, and the pre-Latin root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：genus 最早的英语使用此处无法确定；拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates words that look like genus but are not the same noun; group two compares the ranks and relations around it.
note.cn: 第一组区分看似 genus 却并非同一名词的词；第二组比较它周围的阶元与关系。

entries.definition: Inborn talent or a guiding spirit, from Latin genius 'attendant spirit', tied to gignere. It shares the root but is not the taxonomic rank.
entries.definitionCN: 天生的才能或守护神，来自拉丁 genius「守护灵」，与 gignere 相关。它共用词根，但不是分类阶元。

entries.definition: Authentic, from Latin genuinus 'natural, native'. It looks close but does not descend from genus.
entries.definitionCN: 真正的、地道的，来自拉丁 genuinus「天然的、本生的」。外形相近，却不出自 genus。

entries.definition: The Latin plural of genus, required in technical writing. It is the same word in another number, not another concept.
entries.definitionCN: genus 的拉丁复数，技术写作中必须使用。它是同一个词的另一种数，而非另一个概念。

entries.definition: The case of possession, from the same Latin stock but naming a grammatical function rather than a rank.
entries.definitionCN: 表示所属的格，出自同一拉丁词源，却指语法功能而非分类阶元。

entries.definition: The basic rank contained within a genus; the second word of a binomial.
entries.definitionCN: 包含在属之内的基本阶元；双名法的第二个词。

entries.definition: The rank above genus, grouping several genera that share a deeper common ancestry.
entries.definitionCN: 属之上的阶元，把共享更深共同祖先的若干属聚合起来。

entries.definition: Any named group at any rank. A genus is one kind of taxon, not its synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 任一阶元上被命名的类群。属是分类单元的一种，而非其同义词。

entries.definition: The genus that names and fixes a family; it is a role a genus can play, not a separate rank.
entries.definitionCN: 为科命名并固定其范围的那个属；它是属可以担任的角色，不是另一个阶元。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: genus comes from gignere 'to beget': a genus is a kind traced to a common birth.
normal.cn: genus 出自 gignere「生育」：一个属就是可追溯到共同出生的一类。

normal.en: The plural is genera, and the codes require it; genuses is a sign of amateur use.
normal.cn: 复数是 genera，法规要求如此；genuses 是外行的标志。

normal.en: The binomial is genus plus species epithet, as in Panthera leo.
normal.cn: 双名法是属名加种加词，如 Panthera leo。

normal.en: A family is named after its type genus, which anchors the name.
normal.cn: 科以模式属命名，模式属因此成为名称的锚。

normal.en: Generic drifted from 'of a genus' to 'common to a class' to 'unbranded'.
normal.cn: generic 从「属的」漂移到「整类共有的」，再漂移到「无品牌的」。

abstract.en: Picture a street name that covers many houses, each with its own number.
abstract.cn: 想象一个街名覆盖许多房子，每座房子有自己的门牌号。

abstract.en: Picture a family name shared by cousins who would not recognize each other.
abstract.cn: 想象一个姓氏被彼此不认识的表亲共用。

abstract.en: Picture a box marked 'kind of kinds', holding smaller boxes also marked that way.
abstract.cn: 想象一个写着「类之类」的盒子，里面装着同样标注的小盒子。

examples.en: The genus was split when molecular data showed two unrelated lineages.
examples.cn: 当分子数据显出两条无关谱系时，这个属被拆分了。

examples.en: After the first mention, the genus name is abbreviated to one letter.
examples.cn: 首次提及之后，属名缩写为一个字母。

examples.en: In the old logic, genus and species were relations, not organisms.
examples.cn: 在旧逻辑中，属与种是关系，而不是生物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「gen 生 + us 我们」——同一个根生出来的一群 → genus 属

root: 拉丁 genus, generis「出生、族类、种类」，与 gignere「生育」相关；复数为 genera。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of genus move from the rank itself to its place in a binomial, its logical past, its everyday breadth, its Latin plural, the type genus, the monotypic case and finally the drift visible in generic.
sensesIntro.cn: genus 的八个义项从阶元本身出发，依次是双名法中的位置、逻辑学的前身、日常的宽度、拉丁复数、模式属、单型属，最后是 generic 中可见的语义漂移。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a named box of kinds, sitting inside a larger box and holding smaller ones.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只装着各种「类」的命名盒子，它本身在更大的盒子里，又装着更小的盒子。

branches.en: THE RANK AND ITS ADDRESS: the genus is both a level and the street half of a binomial.
branches.cn: 阶元与地址：属既是一个层级，也是双名法地址中的街道部分。

branches.en: LOGIC AND EVERYDAY USE: containment and 'a kind of' keep the pre-biological meaning alive.
branches.cn: 逻辑与日常：包含关系与「一类」使生物学之前的意义继续存活。

branches.en: THE FORM: the Latin plural genera is obligatory in technical prose.
branches.cn: 形式：技术文献中必须使用拉丁复数 genera。

branches.en: ANCHOR AND EDGE CASE: the type genus fixes a family name, and a monotypic genus adds no information.
branches.cn: 锚点与边界情形：模式属固定科名，单型属则不增加信息。

branches.en: THE DERIVED DRIFT: generic moved from 'of a genus' to 'shared by a class' to 'unbranded'.
branches.cn: 派生漂移：generic 从「属的」变为「整类共有的」，再变为「无品牌的」。

intro.en: Genus is one Latin noun with a double life: a word for birth and lineage, and a word for a kind that contains kinds.
intro.cn: genus 是一个有双重生命的拉丁名词：既指出生与血统，也指容纳更小种类的种类。

latinIntro.en: Latin genus gives genus, genera, generic, generate, generation, genius and genital; gignere is the verb behind them all.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 genus 给出 genus、genera、generic、generate、generation、genius、genital；gignere 是它们背后的动词。

items.example: Genus is both a lineage word and a category word.
items.exampleCN: genus 既是血统词，也是类别词。

items.example: The verb supplies the sense of common birth.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「共同出生」的意思。

items.example: Three genera share the family.
items.exampleCN: 三个属共享这个科。

items.meaning: of a genus; common to a class
items.example: The generic name appears on the label.
items.exampleCN: 标签上写着属名。

items.example: The same root produced generate and generation.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根产生 generate 与 generation。

items.example: Genius is a cousin, not a synonym of genus.
items.exampleCN: genius 是远亲，而非 genus 的同义词。

items.example: Gens names a human lineage, not a taxonomic rank.
items.exampleCN: gens 指人的血统群体，而非分类阶元。

items.example: Greek genesis is a cousin through the same ancient root.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语 genesis 经同一古老词根成为远亲。

definition_zh: 家庭；家人；（生物分类的）科；语系；家族；一族
definition_en: a group of relatives living together or traced to a common ancestor, or a rank in classification grouping related genera
core_image: 旧相册里，三代人围坐在一张长桌旁，每年夏天在同一个屋檐下合影
scene: 旧相册里，三代人围坐在一张长桌旁，那是这个家庭每年夏天固定的合影。 In the old album the whole family sits around one long table, three generations photographed every summer under the same roof.
sceneCN: 这里 family 是「家庭；家人」（第 1 个义项：共同生活的亲属群体）；句意：旧相册里，三代人围坐在一张长桌旁，那是这个家庭每年夏天固定的合影。

pos.zh: 家庭；家人；科（生物分类）；语系；家族；一族

derivatives.zh: 家族主义（以家族利益为先的社会取向）

senses.title: A household of relatives
senses.definition: a group of people related by blood, marriage or adoption, especially parents and their children
senses.definitionCN: 因血缘、婚姻或收养而相关联的一群人，尤指父母与子女
senses.example: The whole family gathers at the same table every summer.
senses.exampleCN: 全家人每年夏天都聚在同一张桌旁。
senses.why: Latin familia first named the household including servants, not only blood kin; English narrowed it toward the kin group while keeping the sense of a shared home.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 familia 最初指包括仆役在内的家户，而不只是血亲；英语把它收窄到亲属群体，同时保留「共同居所」的意思。

senses.title: The taxonomic rank family
senses.definition: the rank below order and above genus, grouping genera that share a common ancestry and structure
senses.definitionCN: 位于目之下、属之上的阶元，把共享祖先与结构的若干属聚合在一起
senses.example: The cat family contains several genera and many species.
senses.exampleCN: 猫科包含若干属与许多物种。
senses.why: Taxonomy borrowed a word for a household because a family of organisms is exactly that: several genera living under one name, traced to one ancestry.
senses.whyCN: 分类学借用了「家庭」这个词，因为一个生物科正是如此：若干属在一个名称下，追溯到同一血统。

senses.title: Family-name suffixes in taxonomy
senses.definition: the conventional endings that mark a family, chiefly -aceae for plants and -idae for animals, built on a type genus
senses.definitionCN: 标记科的惯用词尾，植物主要用 -aceae、动物主要用 -idae，均由模式属构成
senses.example: The ending marks the rank before the reader knows the group.
senses.exampleCN: 读者还未知道类群，词尾就已标出这是科。
senses.why: Codes fix the endings so that rank is visible in the word itself; this is why the same root can appear with -aceae in botany and -idae in zoology.
senses.whyCN: 法规固定词尾，使阶元在词形上就能看出；正因此，同一词根在植物学中作 -aceae，在动物学中作 -idae。

senses.title: A language family
senses.definition: a group of languages descended from one reconstructed ancestor, such as the Indo-European family
senses.definitionCN: 从一个重构祖语分化而来的一组语言，如印欧语系
senses.example: The family tree of the languages was drawn before the genetics was known.
senses.exampleCN: 语言的谱系树在遗传学出现之前就已画出。
senses.why: Linguists used the household image for the same reason biologists did: several daughter languages under one reconstructed parent.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家使用家庭意象的理由与生物学家相同：若干派生语言同属一个重构出的母语。

senses.title: A lineage of notable people
senses.definition: a line of related people, often one that has produced several notable figures over generations
senses.definitionCN: 由亲属连成的一条线，常指几代人中出了若干名人的家族
senses.example: A family of printers kept the type in use for two centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 一个印刷世家让这套字体沿用了两个世纪。
senses.why: The sense is dynastic: the household image extends to inherited craft, name and property rather than to co-residence.
senses.whyCN: 这一义带世家色彩：家庭意象延伸到承袭的手艺、姓氏与财产，而不指共同居住。

senses.title: Nuclear and extended family
senses.definition: the sociological distinction between parents and children alone and a wider kin network including grandparents, aunts and cousins
senses.definitionCN: 社会学上对仅含父母子女与含祖父母、姑舅、表亲等更广亲属网络这两种家庭的区别
senses.example: The survey compared nuclear and extended family households.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查比较了核心家庭与扩展家庭住户。
senses.why: Once the word became an object of study, social science needed to specify its shape, and the pair nuclear/extended did that work.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词成为研究对象，社会科学需要明确它的形态，核心／扩展这一对词便承担了这项工作。

senses.title: A family of mathematical objects
senses.definition: a collection of sets, curves or functions indexed by a parameter and treated as one object of study
senses.definitionCN: 由参数索引、被当作一个对象研究的一组集合、曲线或函数
senses.example: A family of curves fills the plane as the parameter varies.
senses.exampleCN: 随着参数变化，一族曲线铺满平面。
senses.why: Mathematics borrows the household word for a collection whose members are related by a common definition rather than by blood.
senses.whyCN: 数学借用这个家庭词，指成员由共同定义而非血缘联系起来的一个集合。

senses.title: A product or brand family
senses.definition: a set of related products or models marketed under one name and sharing design or platform
senses.definitionCN: 在同一名称下销售、共享设计或平台的一组相关产品或型号
senses.example: The new model joins the same family as the older sedan.
senses.exampleCN: 新车型与旧款轿车属于同一产品系列。
senses.why: Commerce uses the word for the same comfort it gives biology: one name covering several related members, so buyers can predict what they will get.
senses.whyCN: 商业使用这个词，图的是它在生物学中同样的便利：一个名称覆盖若干相关成员，买家因此能预期自己会得到什么。

senses.title: Family as a euphemism or a social unit
senses.titleCN: 作为委婉语或社会单位的「家庭」
senses.definition: an extended use for any close group treated as kin, including chosen families and institutional households
senses.definitionCN: 泛指任何被当作亲属看待的紧密群体，包括自主组成的家庭与机构式家庭
senses.example: The residents call the house their family, and the word is not ironic.
senses.exampleCN: 住户们把这所房子称作他们的家庭，这话并不带讽刺。
senses.why: Because the word carries warmth as well as structure, it can be extended to groups that share care rather than descent; the extension is social, not taxonomic.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个词既含结构也含温度，它可以延伸到以照料而非血统相联的群体；这一延伸是社会性的，不是分类学的。

intro.en: Family comes from Latin familia 'household', which included servants as well as kin. The word entered English through Old French. Dates are approximate, and the deeper origin of famulus is unsettled.
intro.cn: family 来自拉丁 familia「家户」，其中既有亲属也有仆役。该词经古法语进入英语。年代为约数，famulus 的更深来源尚无定论。

items.en: Familia named the whole household, including slaves and dependants, not only blood relatives; the kin sense was present but not exclusive.
items.cn: familia 指整个家户，包括奴隶与依附者，而不只是血亲；亲属义已存在，但并不独占。

items.en: The household word rests on famulus 'servant'. Its deeper origin is not established; a link to Oscan has been suggested but not demonstrated.
items.cn: 这个家户词基于 famulus「仆役」。其更深来源未得到证明；有人提出与奥斯坎语有关，但未获证实。

items.en: Old French famille carried the word into English in the fourteenth century, where it narrowed toward the kin group.
items.cn: 古法语 famille 在 14 世纪把该词带入英语，词义在那里收窄到亲属群体。

items.en: Linnaeus placed familia in his hierarchy in the eighteenth century, and the botanical and zoological codes later fixed its endings.
items.cn: 林奈在 18 世纪把 familia 放进他的层级；植物学与动物学法规后来固定了它的词尾。

items.en: Nineteenth-century sociology made the family an object of study and added the nuclear/extended distinction.
items.cn: 19 世纪社会学把家庭变成研究对象，并加入核心／扩展的区分。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the descent of familia from famulus is generally accepted, but the pre-Latin origin of famulus is unsettled, so any Indo-European form for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：familia 出自 famulus 这一点一般认为是成立的，但 famulus 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，凡为其给出的印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one separates words that look like family; group two compares the household and the ranks around it.
note.cn: 第一组区分外形像 family 的词；第二组比较家庭本身与它周围的阶元。

entries.definition: Well known or close, from Latin familiaris 'of a household'. It is the adjective of family, not a second noun.
entries.definitionCN: 熟悉或亲近的，来自拉丁 familiaris「家户的」。它是 family 的形容词，不是另一个名词。

entries.definition: Relating to family, used especially in medicine and genetics, as in familial traits. It is more technical than familiar.
entries.definitionCN: 与家庭或家族有关的，尤用于医学与遗传学，如家族性性状。比 familiar 更技术化。

entries.definition: A severe shortage of food, from Latin fames 'hunger'. It looks like family but has no household in it.
entries.definitionCN: 严重的食物短缺，来自拉丁 fames「饥饿」。外形像 family，却与家户无关。

entries.definition: A social pattern that puts family interests above individual ones. It is built on family with -ism, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 把家族利益置于个人之上的社会模式。由 family 加 -ism 构成，并非另一词根。

entries.definition: All the people living in one house, related or not; it is the older sense of familia without the kin emphasis.
entries.definitionCN: 同住一屋的全部人，无论是否亲属；它是 familia 的旧义，但不强调血亲。

entries.definition: Relatives by blood or marriage, seen as a network rather than a household; family overlaps with it but also covers co-residence.
entries.definitionCN: 因血缘或婚姻相连的亲属，被看作网络而非家户；family 与它重叠，但也包含共同居住。

entries.definition: A line of descent traced through generations. It stresses ancestry, while family can also mean the people alive now.
entries.definitionCN: 按世代追溯的血统线。它强调祖先，而 family 也可指眼下活着的人。

entries.definition: In taxonomy, the rank above family; a family is one step narrower than an order.
entries.definitionCN: 分类学中科之上的阶元；科比目窄一级。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: familia was a household, famulus a servant: family began as the people under one roof.
normal.cn: familia 是家户，famulus 是仆役：family 最初就是同一屋顶下的人。

normal.en: The taxonomic family sits between order and genus and is named after a type genus.
normal.cn: 生物学的科位于目与属之间，并以模式属命名。

normal.en: Plant families end in -aceae, animal families in -idae; the ending announces the rank.
normal.cn: 植物科以 -aceae 结尾，动物科以 -idae 结尾；词尾直接宣告阶元。

normal.en: A language family and a family of curves use the same household image: related members under one parent.
normal.cn: 语系与曲线族使用同一个家庭意象：相关成员同属一个父项。

normal.en: Familiar and familial are the two adjectives; famine is a false friend from fames 'hunger'.
normal.cn: familiar 与 familial 是两个形容词；famine 则是来自 fames「饥饿」的假朋友。

abstract.en: Picture a long table where the seating chart has been the same for fifty years.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，座次五十年来从未改变。

abstract.en: Picture a surname that arrives before its bearer into every room.
abstract.cn: 想象一个姓氏先于其主人进入每一个房间。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of machines sharing one chassis and one nameplate.
abstract.cn: 想象一排机器共用同一个底盘与同一块铭牌。

examples.en: The family has met at the same table every summer for three generations.
examples.cn: 这个家庭三代人每年夏天都在同一张桌旁相聚。

examples.en: The plant family is named after its largest genus.
examples.cn: 这个植物科以它最大的属命名。

examples.en: Two branches of the language family separated before writing existed.
examples.cn: 这个语系的两支在有文字之前就已分开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「family 家庭」——同一屋檐下的一群人，后来也指同一祖先下的一群生物 → family 家庭；科

root: 拉丁 familia「家户」，基于 famulus「仆役」，famulus 更深来源不确定；经古法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of family extend one household image outward: kin at one table, the taxonomic rank, its fixed endings, a language family, a dynasty, nuclear and extended forms, mathematical families, product lines and chosen families.
sensesIntro.cn: family 的九个义项把同一个家户意象向外延伸：同桌的亲人、生物阶元、固定词尾、语系、世家、核心与扩展家庭、数学族、产品系列，以及自主组成的家庭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one roof over several related members, all answering to one name.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片屋顶罩着若干相关成员，全都在一个名称之下。

branches.en: THE HUMAN HOUSEHOLD: blood kin and chosen families that share care rather than descent.
branches.cn: 人的家户：血亲与以照料而非血统相联的自主家庭。

branches.en: THE TAXONOMIC RANK: a family groups genera and announces itself through -aceae or -idae.
branches.cn: 生物阶元：科聚合若干属，并以 -aceae 或 -idae 自我宣告。

branches.en: DESCENT IN LANGUAGE AND CRAFT: daughter languages and dynasties both use the household tree.
branches.cn: 语言与手艺中的传承：派生语言与世家都使用家户树。

branches.en: THE MEASURABLE FORM: nuclear and extended family give the household a shape that surveys can count.
branches.cn: 可测量的形态：核心与扩展家庭给家户一个调查可以计数的形状。

branches.en: ABSTRACT AND COMMERCIAL SETS: mathematical families and product families share a definition rather than blood.
branches.cn: 抽象与商业集合：数学族与产品族共享定义而非血缘。

intro.en: Family is a household word that spread into taxonomy, linguistics and mathematics without losing its shape: several related members under one name.
intro.cn: family 是一个家户词，扩散到分类学、语言学与数学，却没有失去原有形状：若干相关成员在一个名称之下。

latinIntro.en: Latin familia gives family, familiar, familial and familism; famulus gives the household core, and famine is unrelated, from fames 'hunger'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 familia 给出 family、familiar、familial、familism；famulus 提供家户核心；famine 无关，出自 fames「饥饿」。

items.example: Familia included dependants as well as kin.
items.exampleCN: familia 既含亲属，也含依附者。

items.example: The household word rests on famulus.
items.exampleCN: 这个家户词基于 famulus。

items.example: The family groups several genera.
items.exampleCN: 科把若干属聚合起来。

items.example: A familiar face belongs to the household circle.
items.exampleCN: 熟悉的面孔属于家户圈子。

items.example: Familial traits run in the pedigree.
items.exampleCN: 家族性性状在谱系中传递。

items.example: Rosaceae is built on the type genus Rosa.
items.exampleCN: 蔷薇科由模式属 Rosa 构成。

items.example: Felidae is built on the type genus Felis.
items.exampleCN: 猫科由模式属 Felis 构成。

items.example: Familism shaped the local marriage rules.
items.exampleCN: 家族主义塑造了当地的婚姻规则。

definition_zh: 顺序；次序；命令；订单；目（生物分类）；秩序；修会；勋章；议事规则
definition_en: the arrangement of things in a sequence, a command, or a rank in biological classification
core_image: 一队人按身高排成一行，队首的人手里拿着写有编号的名单
scene: 火车站的值班员按出发时间把列车排成一条队列，旅客照着这个顺序找自己的车次。 At the station the dispatcher arranged the trains in the order of departure, and passengers followed that sequence to find their own service.
sceneCN: 这里 order 是「顺序、次序」（第 1 个义项：事物按先后排列的方式）；句意：值班员按出发时间把列车排成队列，旅客照着这个顺序找自己的车次。

pos.zh: 顺序；次序；秩序；命令；订单；目（生物分类）；修会；勋章

derivatives.zh: 普通的（同出拉丁 ordo 词根）

senses.title: A sequence of things
senses.definition: the way things are arranged one after another, especially according to time, size or importance
senses.definitionCN: 事物按时间、大小或重要性一个接一个排列的方式
senses.example: The dispatcher arranged the trains in the order of departure.
senses.exampleCN: 值班员按出发时间把列车排成队列。
senses.why: Latin ordo first meant a row of threads in a loom, then a row of any kind; a sequence is literally a row read from one end.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 ordo 最初指织机上一排经线，后指任何一排；所谓顺序，字面上就是从一端读过去的一排。

senses.title: A command given to someone
senses.definition: an instruction that must be obeyed, especially one given by an authority
senses.definitionCN: 必须服从的指示，尤指由权威给出的指示
senses.example: The captain gave the order to close the gates.
senses.exampleCN: 队长下令关闭大门。
senses.why: A command is what puts others into an order: the word names both the arrangement and the act of imposing it, which is why a military order and a neat row share one term.
senses.whyCN: 命令就是让别人进入某种次序：这个词既指排列，也指强加排列的动作，因此军令与整齐的一行共用一个词。

senses.title: A purchase request
senses.definition: a request for goods or food to be supplied, or the goods so requested
senses.definitionCN: 要求供应商品或食物的请求，或如此要求的货物
senses.example: She placed an order for two hundred copies.
senses.exampleCN: 她订购了两百册。
senses.why: Commerce extended the word from arrangement to instruction: an order tells a supplier what to arrange and in what quantity.
senses.whyCN: 商业把这个词从排列延伸到指示：订单告诉供货者要安排什么、数量多少。

senses.title: The taxonomic rank order
senses.definition: the rank below class and above family in biological classification
senses.definitionCN: 生物分类中位于纲之下、科之上的阶元
senses.example: The order contains twelve families of beetles.
senses.exampleCN: 这个目包含十二个甲虫科。
senses.why: Taxonomy used the Latin word for a row: an order is a row of families, read in one direction down the hierarchy.
senses.whyCN: 分类学用了这个意为「一排」的拉丁词：一个目就是一排科，沿层级往一个方向读下去。

senses.title: Social or public order
senses.definition: the condition in which rules are obeyed and normal activity can continue
senses.definitionCN: 规则得到遵守、正常活动得以继续的状态
senses.example: The police restored order after the march.
senses.exampleCN: 游行之后警方恢复了秩序。
senses.why: The abstract sense generalizes the row: when everyone is in their place, the whole is in order, and the word names that condition rather than any particular row.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把「一排」一般化：当人人各在其位，整体就有秩序，这个词命名的正是那种状态，而非某一特定行列。

senses.title: A religious order
senses.definition: a body of monks, nuns or friars living under one rule, such as the Franciscans
senses.definitionCN: 遵同一会规生活的修士、修女或托钵僧团体，如方济各会
senses.example: The order ran the hospital for three centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个修会经营了那所医院三百年。
senses.why: A religious order is a body ordered by a rule; the word names both the community and the discipline that holds it together.
senses.whyCN: 修会是一个按会规排序的团体；这个词既指群体，也指维系群体的那套纪律。

senses.title: An honorary order or decoration
senses.definition: a society of people honoured for service, or the decoration that marks membership
senses.definitionCN: 因功绩受表彰者组成的团体，或标记成员身份的勋章
senses.example: He was admitted to the order for public service.
senses.exampleCN: 他因公共服务被授予该勋位。
senses.why: The sense grew from rank: an order is a graded body of members, and the medal is the visible mark of one's place in it.
senses.whyCN: 这一义由「等级」生长出来：勋位是一个分级的成员团体，勋章则是个人在其中的位置可见的标记。

senses.title: A procedural point in a meeting
senses.definition: a question raised about whether the rules of procedure are being followed, as in a point of order
senses.definitionCN: 关于议事规则是否得到遵守而提出的问题，如程序问题
senses.example: A member raised a point of order before the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 表决之前有成员提出了程序问题。
senses.why: Meetings run by rules, and the rules are themselves an order; raising a point of order is asking whether the meeting is still following its own arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 会议依规则进行，而规则本身即是一种秩序；提出程序问题就是问会议是否仍遵守自己的安排。

senses.title: Order of magnitude
senses.definition: a class of scale in which one value is about ten times another, used for rough comparison
senses.definitionCN: 一个值约为另一个值的十倍的尺度等级，用于粗略比较
senses.example: The cost rose by an order of magnitude.
senses.exampleCN: 成本上升了一个数量级。
senses.why: Here order is a step in a graded series: each step multiplies by ten, so the word names a rung rather than a sequence of items.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 order 是分级系列中的一级：每一级乘以十，因此这个词命名的是一级台阶，而不是一串物件。

senses.title: The classical orders of architecture
senses.definition: one of the recognized styles of column and entablature, such as Doric or Corinthian
senses.definitionCN: 多立克、科林斯等被承认的柱与檐部样式之一
senses.example: The facade mixes two architectural orders on one level.
senses.exampleCN: 这面外墙在同一层混用了两种柱式。
senses.why: Vitruvius used ordo for the due arrangement of parts, and the word became the name of each fixed arrangement of column and capital.
senses.whyCN: 维特鲁威用 ordo 指各部分的合宜安排，这个词后来成为柱与柱头每一种固定搭配的名称。

intro.en: Order comes from Latin ordo 'row, rank, arrangement', a third-declension noun whose deeper origin is disputed. It entered English through Old French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: order 来自拉丁 ordo「一排、等级、安排」，是第三变格法名词，其更深来源有争议。该词经古法语进入英语。年代为约数。

items.en: Ordo meant a row, especially a row of threads in a loom, then a rank or an arrangement. The physical row is the oldest image.
items.cn: ordo 指一排，尤其织机上的一排经线，后指等级或安排。物理的一排是最古老的意象。

items.en: The noun is linked to ordiri 'to begin, to lay out a warp'; the connection is accepted, though the verb's own origin is debated.
items.cn: 该名词与 ordiri「开始、铺开经线」相关；这一联系一般认为是成立的，但动词本身的来源仍有争论。

items.en: Old French ordre brought the word into English, where it covered both a row and a command by the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 ordre 把该词带入英语，到 13 世纪已兼指一排与命令。

items.en: The medieval church used order for the ranks of clergy, and the phrase religious order fixed the sense of a community under one rule.
items.cn: 中世纪教会用 order 指神职等级，religious order 一语则固定了「同一会规下的团体」这一义。

items.en: Linnaeus gave order a place in his hierarchy in the eighteenth century, between class and family.
items.cn: 林奈在 18 世纪给 order 在层级中安排了位置，位于纲与科之间。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the link between ordo and ordiri is generally accepted, but the pre-Latin origin of both is unsettled, so Indo-European forms offered for them are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：ordo 与 ordiri 的联系一般认为是成立的，但二者在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，凡为其给出的印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one separates the many English words that descend from ordo; group two compares words of neighbouring meaning.
note.cn: 第一组区分源自 ordo 的众多英语词；第二组比较意思相邻的词。

entries.definition: A number that marks position in a series, such as first or tenth, from ordinalis. It names a place, not a command.
entries.definitionCN: 标记序列位置的数词，如第一、第十，出自 ordinalis。它指位置，不指命令。

entries.definition: Common or usual, from ordinarius 'according to order'. The sense drifted from 'regular' to 'unremarkable'.
entries.definitionCN: 普通、通常的，出自 ordinarius「按次序的」。词义从「合规矩」漂移到「不出奇」。

entries.definition: A decree or regulation, from ordinare 'to arrange'. It is a law that arranges conduct, not a sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 法令或条例，出自 ordinare「安排」。它是安排行为的法规，不是顺序。

entries.definition: To confer holy orders or to decree, from ordinare. It names an authoritative act, not an arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 授予圣职或颁布，出自 ordinare。它指权威性的行为，而非排列。

entries.definition: A series in which one thing follows another, from sequi 'to follow'. It stresses succession, while order can also mean a command or a rank.
entries.definitionCN: 一物接一物形成的系列，出自 sequi「跟随」。它强调接续，而 order 还可指命令或阶元。

entries.definition: The way items are placed relative to one another. It is the result, while order can be the principle behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 各物彼此的摆放方式。它是结果，order 则可以是背后的原则。

entries.definition: A directive from an authority. It matches one branch of order but not the sequence branch.
entries.definitionCN: 权威发出的指示。它对应 order 的一支，而不对应顺序那一支。

entries.definition: A position in a graded scale, as in taxonomic rank. It names the level, while order can name the whole arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 分级尺度中的位置，如分类阶元。它指层级，order 则可指整套安排。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ordo was a row of threads: order is first a row, then a rule that keeps things in rows.
normal.cn: ordo 原是一排经线：order 先是一排，后指使事物各在其排的规则。

normal.en: The same word gives ordinal, ordinary, ordinance and ordain, all built on ordinare 'to arrange'.
normal.cn: 同一个词给出 ordinal、ordinary、ordinance、ordain，皆基于 ordinare「安排」。

normal.en: In biology the order sits between class and family, one rung of the ladder.
normal.cn: 在生物学中，目位于纲与科之间，是梯子上的一级。

normal.en: A point of order asks whether the meeting is following its own rules.
normal.cn: 程序问题问的是会议是否遵守自己的规则。

normal.en: An order of magnitude is one step of ten, a rung rather than a row.
normal.cn: 数量级是以十为一步的一级，是一级台阶而非一排。

abstract.en: Picture a loom where one wrong thread makes the whole pattern shift.
abstract.cn: 想象一台织机，一根线错了，整个花样就移位。

abstract.en: Picture a queue that stays calm because everyone knows their number.
abstract.cn: 想象一支队伍因为人人知道自己的号而保持平静。

abstract.en: Picture a cabinet whose drawers are labelled by size, each ten times the one before.
abstract.cn: 想象一柜按大小标注的抽屉，每一格是前一格的十倍。

examples.en: The names were read out in the order in which they had been received.
examples.cn: 姓名按收到的先后顺序被念出。

examples.en: The general's order reached the front line before dawn.
examples.cn: 将军的命令在黎明前传到了前线。

examples.en: The two families belong to the same order but different superfamilies.
examples.cn: 这两个科属于同一个目，但属于不同的总科。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「or 或者 + der 得」——或者这样排、或者那样排，总得有个次序 → order 顺序；命令

root: 拉丁 ordo, ordinis「一排、等级、安排」，与 ordiri「铺开经线、开始」相关；更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of order follow the row outward: a sequence, a command that imposes sequence, a purchase, a taxonomic rung, social calm, a ruled community, an honour, a procedural question, a factor of ten and a style of columns.
sensesIntro.cn: order 的十个义项沿着「一排」向外走：顺序、强加顺序的命令、订单、生物阶元、社会安定、守会规的团体、勋位、程序问题、十倍一级、柱式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row read from one end, and the rule that keeps it a row.
core.cn: 核心意象：从一端读过去的一排，以及使它保持成一排的那条规则。

branches.en: THE ROW ITSELF: a sequence of items, a factor of ten, or a fixed arrangement of columns.
branches.cn: 一排本身：一串物件、十倍的级差，或柱子的固定搭配。

branches.en: THE INSTRUCTION: a command and a purchase both tell someone what to arrange.
branches.cn: 指示：命令与订单都在告诉别人该安排什么。

branches.en: THE RANK: an order in taxonomy and an honour both place a member on a graded ladder.
branches.cn: 等级：生物学的目与勋位都把成员放在分级的梯子上。

branches.en: THE RULE: social order and a point of order both concern whether rules are being kept.
branches.cn: 规则：社会秩序与程序问题都关心规则是否被遵守。

branches.en: THE COMMUNITY: a religious order is a body held together by one rule.
branches.cn: 团体：修会是由一条会规维系的群体。

intro.en: Order is a Latin noun that English uses for rows, commands and ranks alike; the common thread is arranged position.
intro.cn: order 是拉丁名词，英语用它同时指行列、命令与等级；共同的线索是「被安排的位置」。

latinIntro.en: Latin ordo yields order, ordinal, ordinary, ordinance and ordain; ordinare 'to arrange' is the verb behind the derived forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ordo 衍生 order、ordinal、ordinary、ordinance、ordain；ordinare「安排」是这些派生形式背后的动词。

items.example: Ordo began as a row of threads.
items.exampleCN: ordo 最初指一排线。

items.example: The verb supplies ordering and ordinance.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供 ordering 与 ordinance。

items.example: One word covers the row and the rule.
items.exampleCN: 一个词同时覆盖一排与规则。

items.example: Ordinal numbers answer 'which place'.
items.exampleCN: 序数回答「第几位」。

items.example: The ordinary sense drifted to 'unremarkable'.
items.exampleCN: ordinary 的词义漂移到「不出奇」。

items.example: An ordinance arranges conduct by rule.
items.exampleCN: 法令按规则安排行为。

items.example: Ordain names the act of putting someone in place.
items.exampleCN: ordain 指把某人放到位置上的行为。

items.example: An orderly ward keeps everything in its row.
items.exampleCN: 整齐的病房让一切各在其位。

items.example: A suborder narrows the row of families.
items.exampleCN: 亚目收窄了那一排科。

definition_zh: 班级；课；纲（生物分类）；阶级；类别；等级；类（数学与编程）
definition_en: a group of students taught together, a rank in biological classification, or a set of things sharing a property
core_image: 同一间教室里三十名学生坐在一起，讲台上摊着点名册
scene: 教室里三十名学生坐在同一个班，老师按点名册的顺序依次叫到。 Thirty students sat in one class, and the teacher called their names in the order of the roll.
sceneCN: 这里 class 是「班级」（第 1 个义项：一起上课的学生群体）；句意：教室里三十名学生坐在同一个班，老师按点名册的顺序依次叫到。

pos.zh: 班级；课；纲（生物分类）；阶级；类别；等级

senses.title: A group of students taught together
senses.definition: a set of students who are taught together in one course or at one level
senses.definitionCN: 在同一课程或同一年级一起上课的一组学生
senses.example: Thirty students sat in one class, and the teacher called the roll.
senses.exampleCN: 三十名学生坐在同一个班，老师点了名。
senses.why: Latin classis named a division of the Roman people; the school sense keeps the idea of a division gathered in one place for one purpose.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 classis 指罗马人的一个等级划分；学校义保留了「为同一目的聚集在一处的一群人」这一意思。

senses.title: A period of teaching
senses.definition: a single lesson or period of instruction, or the course it belongs to
senses.definitionCN: 单独的一堂课或一段教学时间，或它所属的课程
senses.example: The chemistry class meets on Tuesday mornings.
senses.exampleCN: 化学课在周二上午上课。
senses.why: A class is both the people and the hour: the same word names the group and the occasion on which it gathers.
senses.whyCN: class 既是人群也是时段：同一个词既指那群人，也指他们聚集的那段时间。

senses.title: The taxonomic rank class
senses.definition: the rank below phylum and above order in biological classification
senses.definitionCN: 生物分类中位于门之下、目之上的阶元
senses.example: The class contains a dozen orders of insects.
senses.exampleCN: 这个纲包含十几个昆虫目。
senses.why: Taxonomy borrowed the Roman division word because a class is exactly that: a division of the living world cut at one level.
senses.whyCN: 分类学借用了罗马的「划分」一词，因为一个纲正是如此：在某一层级上为生物界切出的一刀。

senses.title: A social class
senses.definition: a stratum of society defined by income, occupation, education or birth, often with shared culture
senses.definitionCN: 由收入、职业、教育或出身界定、常共享文化的社会层
senses.example: The novel follows a family moving between two social classes.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说写一个家庭在两个社会阶级之间移动。
senses.why: The Roman classis already ranked citizens by property; the modern sense keeps that grading but attaches it to economic and cultural position.
senses.whyCN: 罗马的 classis 本就按财产给公民分级；现代义保留这种分级，只是把它系于经济与文化位置。

senses.title: A category of things
senses.definition: a set of things grouped together because they share a property, as in a class of compounds
senses.definitionCN: 因共有某一属性而被归在一起的一组事物，如一化合物类
senses.example: A whole class of drugs was withdrawn that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年有一整类药品被撤市。
senses.why: Here the word is nearly 'kind': the shared property does the grouping, and the class is whatever falls under it.
senses.whyCN: 这里的词义近乎「种类」：共有属性完成了分组，纲类就是落入该属性之下的一切。

senses.title: A grade of service or quality
senses.definition: a level of comfort or quality in transport or accommodation, or the corresponding ticket
senses.definitionCN: 交通或住宿中舒适度或品质的等级，或相应的票
senses.example: They travelled first class across the channel.
senses.exampleCN: 他们坐头等舱横渡海峡。
senses.why: Grading passengers by fare is the old ranking sense applied to comfort: each class is a division with its own price and its own carriage.
senses.whyCN: 按票价给乘客分级，是古老的分级义用在舒适度上：每一等都是一个划分，有自己的价格与车厢。

senses.title: An equivalence class in mathematics
senses.definition: the set of all objects that are equivalent to one another under a given relation
senses.definitionCN: 在给定关系下彼此等价的所有对象构成的集合
senses.example: Every integer belongs to exactly one residue class modulo seven.
senses.exampleCN: 每个整数恰好属于模七的一个剩余类。
senses.why: Mathematics needed a precise name for 'everything that counts as the same', and class supplied it: a box holding all objects the relation cannot tell apart.
senses.whyCN: 数学需要为「所有算作相同的东西」取一个精确名称，class 提供了它：一只装着关系无法区分的一切对象的盒子。

senses.title: A class in object-oriented programming
senses.definition: a template that defines the data and behaviour of the objects created from it
senses.definitionCN: 定义由其创建的对象的数据与行为的模板
senses.example: The class defines a method that every instance inherits.
senses.exampleCN: 这个类定义了一个每个实例都继承的方法。
senses.why: Programming borrowed the word for a set of objects sharing structure: the class is the category, and each object is a member of it.
senses.whyCN: 编程借用了这个词，指共享结构的一组对象：类是那个类别，每个对象是它的成员。

senses.title: A class interval in statistics
senses.definition: one of the ranges into which data are grouped for a frequency table, such as 10 to 19
senses.definitionCN: 为编制频数表而把数据分入的若干区间之一，如十到十九
senses.example: The first class interval contains the youngest respondents.
senses.exampleCN: 第一个组距包含最年轻的受访者。
senses.why: Statistics cuts a continuous range into ordered boxes called classes; the word's old sense of a division survives in the technical phrase.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把连续范围切成有序的盒子，称为类；这个词古老的「划分」义在术语中存活下来。

senses.title: To place something in a category
senses.definition: the verb sense: to assign a person or thing to a class, sometimes with a judgement attached
senses.definitionCN: 动词义：把人或物归入某一类，有时带有评判
senses.example: Critics classed the film as a comedy, though it ends in grief.
senses.exampleCN: 评论者把这部电影归为喜剧，尽管它以悲伤收尾。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into an act: someone decides which box a thing goes in, and that decision can be disputed.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：某人决定某物进哪只盒子，而这个决定可以被争论。

intro.en: Class comes from Latin classis, a division of the Roman people, probably from calare 'to call'. It entered English through French classe. Dates are approximate, and the deeper origin is disputed.
intro.cn: class 来自拉丁 classis，指罗马人的一个等级划分，可能出自 calare「召集」。该词经法语 classe 进入英语。年代为约数，更深来源有争议。

items.en: Classis named a division of the citizen body, and also a fleet; the two senses coexisted because both were organized divisions.
items.cn: classis 指公民群体的一个划分，也指舰队；两义并存，因为二者都是被组织起来的划分。

items.en: The noun is often derived from calare 'to call, summon', which would make a class a body called together. The derivation is probable rather than proven.
items.cn: 该名词常被追溯到 calare「召集、呼唤」，若如此则一个等级就是被召集起来的一群人。这一派生属可能，而非已证。

items.en: Old French classe brought both the school sense and the social sense into English.
items.cn: 古法语 classe 把学校义与社会义一并带入英语。

items.en: Linnaeus gave class a fixed place between phylum and order, and the botanical and zoological codes kept it.
items.cn: 林奈给 class 在门与目之间固定了位置，植物学与动物学法规沿用至今。

items.en: Nineteenth-century social theory made class a central analytical term, tying it to property and labour rather than to summons.
items.cn: 19 世纪社会理论把阶级变成核心分析术语，把它系于财产与劳动，而非「召集」。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the link to calare is widely accepted but not demonstrated, and the pre-Latin origin of classis is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：与 calare 的联系被广泛接受，却未获证实；classis 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论。

note.en: Group one separates words that look like class; group two compares categories, ranks and grades.
note.cn: 第一组区分外形像 class 的词；第二组比较类别、等级与品级。

entries.definition: Of the highest standard, from classicus 'of the first class'. It grades quality rather than grouping students.
entries.definitionCN: 最高水准的，出自 classicus「头等的」。它评定品质，而不是把学生分组。

entries.definition: To sort into classes, from classis plus facere. It names the act that produces a class.
entries.definitionCN: 归入类别，来自 classis 加 facere。它指产生类别的动作。

entries.definition: Stylish or elegant, a colloquial descendant of class in its 'high grade' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 有格调、优雅的，是 class「高级」义的口语派生。

entries.definition: A loud conflict or disagreement, probably imitative in origin. It looks close but has no classis in it.
entries.definitionCN: 响亮的冲突或不一致，来源可能为拟声。外形相近，却与 classis 无关。

entries.definition: Any set of things grouped by a shared feature, from Greek kategoria. It is broader and less institutional than class.
entries.definitionCN: 按共有特征归在一起的一组事物，来自希腊 kategoria。比 class 更宽、更少制度色彩。

entries.definition: A rank of quality or a school year. It stresses level rather than the group that occupies it.
entries.definitionCN: 品质等级或年级。它强调水平，而非占据该水平的那群人。

entries.definition: In taxonomy, the rank immediately above class; a class is a division of an order.
entries.definitionCN: 分类学中紧接在纲之上的阶元；纲是目的一个划分。

entries.definition: A layer of society, from Latin stratum 'something spread'. It is a geological metaphor used in sociology.
entries.definitionCN: 社会中的一个层，来自拉丁 stratum「铺开之物」。这是用于社会学的地质学隐喻。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: classis was a Roman division: a class is a division of people, organisms or things.
normal.cn: classis 是罗马人的一个划分：class 就是人、生物或事物的一道划分。

normal.en: The school, social and taxonomic senses all keep the shape 'a division at one level'.
normal.cn: 学校义、社会义与分类义都保留「某一层级上的一道划分」这一形状。

normal.en: classify is classis + facere, literally 'to make a division'; classification is its noun.
normal.cn: classify 是 classis 加 facere，字面为「做出划分」；classification 是其名词。

normal.en: In the ranked ladder, class sits between phylum and order.
normal.cn: 在分级梯子上，纲位于门与目之间。

normal.en: In programming, a class is a template, and each object is an instance of that class.
normal.cn: 在编程中，类是一个模板，每个对象是该类的一个实例。

abstract.en: Picture a school corridor with doors numbered by year, each room holding its own roll.
abstract.cn: 想象一条学校走廊，门按年级编号，每间房有自己的名册。

abstract.en: Picture a spreadsheet where every row belongs to exactly one coloured band.
abstract.cn: 想象一张表格，每一行恰好属于一条彩色带。

abstract.en: Picture a set of keys cut from one blank: same shape, different copies.
abstract.cn: 想象用同一个坯子配出的一串钥匙：形状相同，副本各异。

examples.en: The class of 2019 still meets every summer.
examples.cn: 2019 届毕业班每年夏天仍相聚。

examples.en: Biologists place the insects in a class of their own.
examples.cn: 生物学家把这些昆虫放在它们自己的一个纲里。

examples.en: The survey split incomes into five class intervals.
examples.cn: 这项调查把收入分成五个组距。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「class 课」——同一堂课里的人，也是同一层级里的一群 → class 班级；纲；阶级

root: 拉丁 classis「罗马人的一个等级划分；舰队」，可能出自 calare「召集」；经法语 classe 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of class all rest on one shape, a division cut at one level: students, a lesson, a taxonomic rank, a social stratum, a category, a grade of travel, a mathematical box, a programming template, a statistical interval and the act of assigning.
sensesIntro.cn: class 的十个义项都建立在同一个形状上，即在某一层级切出的一道划分：学生、一节课、生物阶元、社会层、类别、出行等级、数学盒子、编程模板、统计组距，以及归类的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a box cut out of a larger whole at one level, with everyone inside sharing a mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：从更大整体中在某一层级切出的一只盒子，里面的人都带着同一个标记。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL DIVISION: the group and the hour are two faces of one word.
branches.cn: 学校里的划分：人群与课时是同一个词的两面。

branches.en: THE TAXONOMIC CUT: class is a division of a phylum, above the order.
branches.cn: 分类学的一刀：纲是门的一个划分，位于目之上。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL LADDER: class as a stratum, and class as a grade of comfort.
branches.cn: 社会的梯子：阶级作为一个层，class 也指舒适等级。

branches.en: FORMAL BOXES: categories, equivalence classes, programming templates and statistical intervals are all the same cut made precise.
branches.cn: 形式化的盒子：类别、等价类、编程模板与统计组距都是同一刀被精确化。

branches.en: THE ACT: to class something is to decide which box it goes into.
branches.cn: 动作：把某物归类，就是决定它进哪只盒子。

intro.en: Class is a Roman division word that became a school word, a social word and a taxonomic word without changing its shape.
intro.cn: class 是一个罗马的划分词，后来成为学校词、社会词与分类词，形状始终未变。

latinIntro.en: Latin classis yields class, classic and classify; facere supplies the -fy of classify and the -fication of classification.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 classis 衍生 class、classic、classify；facere 提供 classify 的 -fy 与 classification 的 -fication。

items.example: Classis named a division before it named a classroom.
items.exampleCN: classis 先指划分，后指教室。

items.example: To classify is literally to make a class.
items.exampleCN: classify 字面就是「做出一个类」。

items.example: One class is one cut through a larger whole.
items.exampleCN: 一个 class 就是对更大整体的一刀。

items.example: Clerks classify each new file on arrival.
items.exampleCN: 新文件到达时由职员归类。

items.meaning: the act or result of sorting
items.example: Classification precedes the shelf it fills.
items.exampleCN: 分类先于它所占的那层架子。

items.example: Classicus graded quality, not pupils.
items.exampleCN: classicus 评定的是品质，不是学生。

items.example: Classy is the colloquial descendant of 'first class'.
items.exampleCN: classy 是「头等」的口语后裔。

items.example: A classless society is defined by the absence of strata.
items.exampleCN: 无阶级社会以层的缺席来定义。

items.meaning: the room where a class meets
items.example: The classroom is named after the group, not the building.
items.exampleCN: 教室因那群人而得名，而非因建筑。

definition_zh: 门（生物分类中位于界之下、纲之上的阶元）
definition_en: a primary rank in biological classification, below kingdom and above class, defined mainly by body plan
core_image: 博物馆展厅按身体构型把动物分到不同的门，每个展厅入口挂着一块说明牌
scene: 博物馆的展厅按身体构型把动物分类，每个入口挂着一块说明牌。 The museum's galleries place each animal group in a separate phylum by body plan, with a label at every entrance.
sceneCN: 这里 phylum 是「门」（第 1 个义项：界之下、纲之上的主要分类阶元）；句意：博物馆展厅按身体构型把每一类动物放进一个单独的门，每个入口挂着说明牌。

senses.title: The primary rank below kingdom
senses.titleCN: 位于界之下的主要阶元
senses.definition: a major division of a kingdom, grouping classes that share a fundamental body plan
senses.definitionCN: 界之下的一个主要划分，把共享基本身体构型的若干纲聚合起来
senses.example: The museum groups animals into different phyla by body plan.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆按身体构型把动物分到不同的门。
senses.why: New Latin phylum was taken from Greek phylon 'race, tribe'; the rank names a whole branch of the living world rather than a single kind.
senses.whyCN: 新拉丁语 phylum 取自希腊语 phylon「族、支系」；这个阶元命名的是一整条生物界的支系，而非单个种类。

senses.title: A body plan as the defining mark
senses.titleCN: 以身体构型为界定标志
senses.definition: the level at which animals are separated by overall architecture, such as radial or bilateral symmetry and the presence of a backbone
senses.definitionCN: 按整体构造把动物分开的层级，如辐射或两侧对称、有无脊椎
senses.example: A new body plan is what justifies a new phylum.
senses.exampleCN: 一个新的身体构型，正是设立一个新门的理由。
senses.why: Unlike a species, a phylum is not defined by breeding but by architecture: what is shared is a way of being built, and that is why the rank is so deep.
senses.whyCN: 与物种不同，门不是由繁殖而是由构造界定：共享的是一种建造方式，这正是这个阶元如此深层的原因。

senses.title: The botanical equivalent: division
senses.titleCN: 植物学中的对应等级：部
senses.definition: in botanical nomenclature, the rank called division or divisio, which corresponds to phylum in zoology
senses.definitionCN: 植物命名法中称为部（divisio）的等级，相当于动物学中的门
senses.example: Botanists traditionally say division where zoologists say phylum.
senses.exampleCN: 动物学家说门的地方，植物学家传统上说部。
senses.why: Two codes grew separately, so the same level carries two names; recognizing the equivalence prevents a reader from thinking a rank is missing.
senses.whyCN: 两套法规各自成长，因此同一层级有两个名称；认清这种对应，读者才不会以为少了一级。

senses.title: The plural phyla
senses.definition: the New Latin plural used in English for several phyla, following the Greek neuter pattern
senses.definitionCN: 按希腊中性模式构成的拉丁复数，英语中用于指多个门
senses.example: Thirty-two phyla are recognized in the animal kingdom.
senses.exampleCN: 动物界现被承认的有三十二个门。
senses.why: The plural is a Greek-style -a form, not an English -s; technical writing keeps it because the codes do.
senses.whyCN: 复数是希腊式的 -a 形式，而非英语的 -s；技术写作沿用，因为法规如此。

senses.title: The major animal phyla in teaching
senses.titleCN: 教学中列举的主要动物门
senses.definition: the short list of well-known phyla used to introduce animal diversity, such as arthropods, molluscs and chordates
senses.definitionCN: 用于介绍动物多样性的少数知名门，如节肢动物、软体动物与脊索动物
senses.example: The course covers eight phyla in one semester.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课一学期讲八个门。
senses.why: Teaching compresses diversity into a handful of names; the short list is a pedagogical selection, not a claim that the others do not exist.
senses.whyCN: 教学把多样性压缩成少数名称；这份短名单是教学上的选取，并不表示其余的门不存在。

senses.title: Phylum boundaries under molecular revision
senses.titleCN: 分子数据修订下的门界
senses.definition: the redrawing of phylum limits when sequence data show that traditional body plans hide deeper relationships
senses.definitionCN: 当序列数据显示传统身体构型掩盖了更深关系时，对门的界线所作的重新划定
senses.example: Molecular data merged two phyla that had been separated for a century.
senses.exampleCN: 分子数据把两个已分隔一个世纪的门合并了。
senses.why: A body plan can converge, so similarity of architecture is not proof of kinship; when sequences disagree with shape, the rank's boundary is reopened.
senses.whyCN: 身体构型可能趋同，因此构造相似并不能证明亲缘；当序列与外形不一致，门的界线就会被重新打开。

senses.title: A phylum-level lineage in phylogenetics
senses.titleCN: 系统发生学中的门级支系
senses.definition: a deep branch of the tree of life, treated as a phylum-level lineage even before a formal rank is assigned
senses.definitionCN: 生命树上的一个深层分支，在正式阶元尚未确定之前就被当作门级支系
senses.example: The uncultured microbes form a phylum-level lineage of their own.
senses.exampleCN: 这些尚未培养的微生物自成一个门级支系。
senses.why: Sequences can reveal a deep branch before anyone can name its anatomy, so the word is used for the branch itself rather than for a described body plan.
senses.whyCN: 序列可以在任何人描述其解剖结构之前就揭示一个深层分支，因此这个词被用于分支本身，而非已被描述的身体构型。

senses.title: No fixed suffix for phylum names
senses.definition: the convention that phylum names are not governed by a single ending, unlike families, so their form must be learned name by name
senses.definitionCN: 门名不像科名那样由单一词尾管束，其形式须逐个记诵的惯例
senses.example: Phylum names have no common ending, so each one must be learned separately.
senses.exampleCN: 门名没有共同词尾，因此只能一个一个地记。
senses.why: Codes standardize the endings of families and orders, but phylum names are old and irregular; the absence of a rule is itself the rule to remember.
senses.whyCN: 法规统一了科与目的词尾，门名却古老而不规则；没有规则，正是需要记住的规则。

intro.en: Phylum is a New Latin noun coined from Greek phylon 'race, tribe, stock', which derives from phyein 'to grow'. Ernst Haeckel introduced it as a rank in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: phylum 是依希腊语 phylon「族、支系、种系」造的新拉丁语名词，后者出自 phyein「生长」。海克尔在 19 世纪把它引入为分类阶元。年代为约数。

items.en: Phylon meant 'race, tribe, stock', and phyle named a tribe or a military division of the Athenian state.
items.cn: phylon 意为「族、部落、种系」，phylē 指雅典城邦的部落或军事划分。

items.en: The word is tied to phyein 'to grow, bring forth', and to physis 'nature'. The sense is a stock that has grown from one root.
items.cn: 该词与 phyein「生长、产生」及 physis「自然」相关。其义为从一个根生长出来的一支种系。

items.en: Ernst Haeckel introduced phylum as a rank above class, using the Greek word for a stock or tribe.
items.cn: 海克尔于 1866 年引入 phylum 作为纲之上的阶元，用的是希腊语中表示种系或部落的词。
